title: Local Contracts
text:
## Local Contracts

- Scenario-owned pictures, icons, portraits, sounds, and map art remain package media. Built-in resource families enter this folder only through an exact-commit catalog with explicit ownership, license, modifications, and byte hashes; scenario packages may override an exact application key.
- The front-door Realmz Rebuilt intro is app-owned project-owner-supplied art, not scenario media. Commit its byte-exact native Ogg Theora/Vorbis stream and record the exact source hash, byte length, dimensions, frame rate, duration, codecs, audio shape, and looping contract in `ui/intro/intro-video.json`. Its app-owned SpriteCook ornament remains separate generated chrome; `ui/spritecook-assets.json` records the style asset, generation job, source hash, transparent-center derivation, dimensions, and production hash.
- Verified base-game UI controls and map markers may enter only through the exact-commit catalog/importer. Preserve each imported source bitmap byte-for-byte. Runtime footer composition may crop or mask the untouched source to isolate its semantic icon while replacing embedded donor captions and hotkeys with live project typography. Record semantic evidence per asset: donor-scene use for controls or pinned Castle resource-fork ownership plus source/control-flow for built-in PICTs and CICNs. A numeric resource ID without its owning fork is insufficient provenance.
- The ordinary map-marker set is exact built-in CICN 175 west, 186 east, and 178 camp. Camp presentation preserves the prior mounted facing for restoration; it never derives or repaints a tent icon.
- Generated structural chrome must contain no text, symbols, scenario content, or executable metadata. App-owned status and command glyphs are separate generated UI categories: each may depict one semantic symbol, contain no embedded words, record its SpriteCook asset/job provenance and exact hashes in `ui/spritecook-assets.json`, and render only at native integer scale. Generate a command glyph only after the stock application library and source control flow prove that no owned icon exists.
- The cataloged spell-target plates remain byte-exact donor evidence. Runtime target badges may key away only their neutral gray plate pixels through `classic_spell_target_text.gdshader`, preserving the original saturated gradient lettering over native Rebuilt inset slate; the source PNGs are never rewritten or presented as application chrome.
- Command bitmap provenance is semantic, not stylistic: current donor controls remain implementation leads unless the catalog proves their Castle resource ownership. App-owned bevel, focus, disabled chrome, and live captions unify footer controls while the compositor samples only the icon portion of untouched donor files. Ordinary Encounter uses exact application PICT 180 as source evidence and masks only the surrounding legacy plate; Heal uses the separately provenance-bound generated glyph because source inspection proves its Castle control has no icon payload. A generated reconstruction cannot be called exact without a supplied reference and explicit provenance.
- Selected SpriteCook chrome records the remote asset ID, generation label, source hash, deterministic derivation, and production hash. Runtime slate uses its deterministic cosine-feathered seamless derivative; frame centers and complete bevel bounds contain that same native-scale tile. The exploration rail is alpha-cropped and reduced to its recorded production dimensions, then centered at no more than 1x over the tiled slate gutter. Opposite tile edges must match exactly, no container may stretch a stone center, and generated frame corners must remain opaque.
- Selected SpriteCook status and command glyphs remain their direct production outputs. The save disk, journal book/quill, and Heal glyph retain their recorded native dimensions and may not be stretched to a shared display size.
- Original controls use nearest-neighbor filtering at exact 1x/2x only. Fonts ship with pinned source, hashes, and licenses and introduce no runtime network dependency. `Theldrow-Classic.fnt` and its atlas are deterministic, metric-preserving conversions of licensed Castle `FONT` 1601; keep that native strike monochrome, nearest-neighbor sampled, and unstretched as reference evidence. `Theldrow-Classic-Vector.ttf` preserves Samuel's scalable CC0 outlines as reference. Runtime Classic text uses deterministic `Theldrow-Rebuilt.ttf`: the approved Pen letter contours, machine-verified production-sheet proportions, sidebearings, and mixed-case optical weight, exact FONT 1601 horizontal advances, zero kerning, and pinned OFL Grenze Gotisch numerals, punctuation, and extended utility glyphs. Numerals keep their Castle advances but are normalized to the declared cap-height figure zone. The reviewed lowercase `h` deliberately overshoots both the cap line and baseline; all other vertical variants follow their declared class zones. Black Chancery, ChicagoFLF, and Castle's Inter Geneva substitute retain their exact pinned bytes. Alegreya remains the readable-mode fallback family.
- The licensed Searching atlas remains byte-exact and records its eight-frame row in the manifest. Exact Torch frame files also remain byte-exact; presentation may key only each asset's documented legacy neutral-gray matte colors while composing them onto Rebuilt chrome.
- Integrated sounds retain exact `snd ` IDs and load from Godot-imported WAV resources. The generated manifest and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` preserve the Castle commit, source fork, copyright, license, and decoding/resampling modification.
- Integrated stock music retains eleven unique Castle modules and loads them from Godot-imported looping Ogg resources. Desert, Swamp, and Snow remain distinct playlist preferences but resolve the Outdoor module; `classic-application-music.json` records exact module commits and hashes, deterministic OpenMPT/FFmpeg conversion settings, output hashes, durations, and the pinned-MADG-to-later-standard-MOD Outdoor replacement. Custom 1–3 are scenario-owned exact resources; never copy them into the application bank.
- Integrated combat CIcons retain exact `cicn` IDs and native dimensions. The selected catalog is limited to source-backed active cues, result effects 159–167, bounded death-effect candidates 2015–2019, and existing spell cast/resolution frames 12000–12127. Standard spells with `lookStart` zero make Castle request the absent 11992–11999 family; presentation reports that exact unavailable identity rather than substituting art. Scenario media overrides the same exact key. Red pixels or numeric adjacency alone do not establish blood, gore, or a semantic identity.
- Integrated item CIcons retain the exact shared Data ID record identity, application-owned stock-supply identities referenced by active-scenario `Data NI`, and Castle's unidentified-range substitutes from `lookupicon`. Core view/request projection selects the player-knowable exact key; Inventory, Equipment, Trade, Shop, and Treasure render that key without exposing its numeric resource ID. Presentation never derives an icon from an item stable ID.
- Keep only selected production assets. Rejected candidates remain external evidence.

title: Local gate
text:
## Local gate

```powershell
./tools/verify.ps1
```

The aggregate gate imports the project headlessly, validates all scripts, runs typed GDScript tests, checks forbidden core dependencies, verifies the mirrored schema and synthetic package hashes/provenance, checks the differential ledger and application workflow inventory, and runs `git diff --check`.

Regenerate the deterministic application-completeness report with `./tools/verify_application_workflow_inventory.ps1 -Write`; normal verification uses `-Check` and fails if the report is stale. Clean Castle, Remake, and Providence roots may be supplied to validate every external path and symbol against the pinned commits.

For Tier 1, use `./tools/run_tests.ps1 -Suite <path-fragment> -Case <test-name-fragment>`. Pass arrays such as `-Suite @("<suite-a>", "<suite-b>") -Case @("<case-a>", "<case-b>")` to select a union in one Godot process. Named cases require an owning suite filter so unrelated suites are never instantiated. Every supplied filter must match, case execution is reported and timed individually, and suites with shared fixture arguments prepare them once through the test-case contract. Focused processes have a 120-second default budget and are terminated as a process tree on timeout. Do not rerun an unchanged timed-out command: narrow its case filters or investigate the named slow case first. For Tier 2, use `./tools/verify_workflow.ps1 -Suite @("<fragment-a>") -Case @("<case-a>", "<case-b>")`; it uses the same streaming/budgeted runner, then performs the conditional architecture check, differential/inventory checks, scope checks, and whitespace check. Clean-reference roots are a Tier 3 input. Release and Tier 3 closeout evidence uses the complete suite directly and is not constrained by the focused timeout.

The Tier 2 helper is not a substitute for the batch closeout gate. Do not add unrelated suites, invoke MCP, or regenerate source-intelligence artifacts merely to make a focused workflow appear comprehensive.

title: Local Contracts
text:
## Local Contracts

- The VM is presentation-independent and serializable at every interaction yield.
- Scenario execution depends only on core models/contracts; immutable instruction and program records cross inward from `src/core/scenario` without importing executor behavior back into core.
- Domain mutations execute through one session-owned `RealmzRuntimeApi`; there are no Godot ports or dynamic GDScript fallbacks.
- `RealmzRuntimeApi` is the single VM boundary and delegates source-backed work to typed domain executors under `runtime/operations`; those executors cannot bypass `GameState`, `RealmzRules`, or the session RNG.
- Classic GOSUB depth is 20. Safe Action call depth is 32, program size 4,096 nodes, arrays 256 entries, and execution 65,536 steps.
- Unknown instructions, IDs, capabilities, actions, and response shapes fail explicitly.
- Safe Scenario Actions may request explicit elapsed minutes through the time capability, but they do not expose the player-facing Camp/Rest workflow as a capability. Camp mode, held Rest pulses, random interruption, and movement departure remain session-owned typed intents and continuations.
- Packages cannot override `realmz.*`; campaign actions use `scenario.<campaign>.*`.
- A Scenario Action call is an ordinary AP/Encounter timeline entry. Authoring gaps and behavior anchors are not runtime concepts.
- Runtime instruction forms are preserved `ClassicAction` records and typed `CallScenarioAction` records. Safe bytecode is compiler output, never Providence editor state.
- The session owns the active VM, action state, runtime API, and post-move continuation. VM snapshots include Classic and Safe frames, origin, trace, and any pending typed interaction.
- VM frames and program transfers carry a closed `ScenarioExecutionContext`; raw context dictionaries never enter live execution. The context codec preserves only declared trigger, application, encounter, combat, and program-transfer provenance and rejects unknown saved fields.
- A saved Classic program replacement is resolved once when a frame starts. Redirecting the active AP changes that frame explicitly; neither behavior rewrites immutable package programs.
- Classic XAP transfers inherit the issuing frame's AP origin/context. Loading macro code cannot erase the trigger identity required by source-backed operations such as opcode 25.
- Battle opcodes resolve the Classic battle ID from Extra Code slot zero when a row is present; the action operand is only the direct-ID form when no Extra Code row exists.
- Battle-round and monster-death macros run as serializable nested VM frames. A death macro receives the defeated combatant ID and must complete before occupancy, allegiance, and battle outcome are finalized; `FD-COMBAT-007` retains the pending subject's footprint so CODE 119 revival remains positioned and saveable. Spell-triggered death macros drain from the combat state's save-owned queue before the issuing caster advances. The host may not clear allegiance merely because a queued macro completed; an authored operation such as opcode 119 owns that mutation.
- Typed combat-action requests expose all eight session-probed player directions and exact disabled reasons. In melee mode, an opposed occupied direction carries the stable hostile combatant identity and remains a typed move response; the core resolves Guard-before-contact and collision melee without moving. Missile Target/Fire remains a distinct actor-target response. The runtime API does not infer targets, positions, allegiance, or movement legality from presentation state.
- A manual typed combat-move response may carry the boolean `autoSwitchToMelee` application preference. The runtime defaults absent legacy responses to false, rejects malformed values, and delegates the exact projectile-profile, manual-actor, Guard-order, switch, sound, cost, and attack transaction to `CombatFlow`; it never applies the preference to direct or automatic actions. Preference-off hostile projectile contact plays Castle warning sound 6000 and returns to the unchanged combat request rather than failing the scenario continuation.
- Typed combat-action requests expose the battle-owned character weapon mode, exact legal mode switch, and source-owned ordinary projectile targets. Missile mode omits melee attacks; Fire carries the actor and selected stable target ID and remains disabled with an exact reason for unsupported projectile classes or failed range/LOS/resource gates.
- Typed combat-action requests expose source-admitted spell and power choices without eagerly expanding their actor or coordinate targets. Automatic groups carry no fabricated target ID; spatial types 3 and 4 carry a rules-owned Data AD shape, ordered offsets, and default battlefield coordinate, and the response returns only the chosen coordinate and rotation. The runtime API never rebuilds area masks, range, LOS, or affected actors from presentation state; it submits the selected target to the authoritative core probe once.
- Typed combat-action requests also expose source-probed fixed-power charged spell-item options with exact item-instance, spell, power, and actor or automatic-group target identity. Responses return only those stable IDs; the runtime revalidates and commits charge/load, action resources, sound, effect, and continuation through `CombatFlow`. It never treats an item use as a memorized spell or accepts an arbitrary script fallback.
- Typed combat requests expose rules-owned Auto Turn, Delay, Bandage-recipient, and Turn Undead probes plus sorted persistent-Auto IDs. A `set_auto` response changes only the named living party character, and enabling the active actor may enter the same bounded automatic activation transaction immediately. The runtime preserves mandatory VM/death-macro yields and never automates across them.
- Classic opcode 1 preserves the message operand sign as control flow. A positive message yields a typed, saveable `acknowledge` request for the dedicated Classic textbox and may record its representable Data SD2 identity through an explicit `takeNote` response; a negative message publishes its presentation event and continues without a click or fabricated note action. The runtime accepts only message IDs 0 through 2,999 for journal discovery under `FD-MAPS-002`; Auto Note remains a separate preferences gap.
- A Classic or Safe time operation and Classic opcode 17/18 spell that changes an age band yields a typed `age_update`; its runtime continuation owns the ordered remaining updates and resumes the exact issuing VM frame only after every response.
- Classic opcode 3 treats zero option IDs as the standard Yes/No pair. Nonzero IDs resolve through the package's Data OD option-label table, with ordinary message lookup used only for old-format packages that have no option-label table.
- Thief encounters and ability-reading opcodes query the character's trained-ability array. They never substitute the separate twelve-slot racial combat-modifier array; the unauthored fifteenth trained slot remains zero under `FD-CHARACTER-001`.
- Classic opcode 30 filters candidates using each iterated character's own attribute or trained ability and applies a negative index once as select-on-failure under `FD-SCENARIO-001`; Castle's action-slot alias and attribute-only double inversion are not reproduced. Opcode 31 preserves the separately observed undefined-attribute path: it asks for one living character, consumes one Rand(25) draw, keeps that identity selected, and continues without either XAP. title: Godot MCP Pro workflow
text:
## Godot MCP Pro workflow

After the initial bootstrap, change project settings through MCP/editor project-setting operations rather than editing `project.godot` directly. For each playable slice:

1. Open or build the scene using editor tools.
2. Inspect editor errors.
3. Call `play_scene`.
4. Simulate input or run a test scenario.
5. Inspect runtime state and screen text.
6. Capture screenshots.
7. Call `stop_scene`.

For interaction slices, inspect the pending request ID before responding, save while the request is pending, resume it once, restore that save, and resume it again. This proves that presentation is returning typed responses and that the issuing VM frame—not a UI callback—is the continuation authority.

Runtime operations before `play_scene` are invalid. Use CLI discovery with `node <server>/build/cli.js --help` when MCP tools are not exposed in the current client.

The vendored MCP plugin does not initialize in a headless editor process. This keeps headless verification from claiming and removing the live editor's temporary runtime-service autoloads, so focused and aggregate checks may run while the MCP editor remains open. The MCP scene-save command can still emit Godot progress-dialog errors while handling its deferred request; restart the editor before the final clean error inspection after MCP-authored scene changes.

Release presets exclude `addons/godot_mcp`, `.mcp.json`, tests, tools, docs, contract mirrors, local artifacts, and ignored reference worktrees. `tools/verify_export_contract.ps1` enforces those exclusions and the ETC2/ASTC import required by the universal macOS preset; Godot's generated export metadata remains part of a valid pack.

The repository defines `Windows Desktop`, `Linux`, and `macOS` release presets. CI runs the same import, typed test, architecture, contract, and export gates on native runners; a configured matrix is not cross-platform evidence until those jobs pass.

`tools/corpus_acceptance.ps1` accepts caller-supplied package/route/report descriptors so commercial campaign locations remain external. `tools/route_acceptance.gd` may execute a named compiled macro directly for an unplaced ED3/XAP checkpoint; that proves the macro path and never upgrades it to placed-map reachability.

title: FD-SCENARIO-001 — Per-character opcode 30 checks
text:
## FD-SCENARIO-001 — Per-character opcode 30 checks

- Affected rule: Classic opcode 30 filtering of tracked characters by an attribute or trained ability.
- Castle evidence: commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`, `src/realmz_orig/newland.c`, `newland`, lines 2426–2500. The loop advances `loop` through tracked characters but reads `c[t]`, where `t` is the action-slot cursor. Negative attribute checks invert inside the attribute branch and then invert the complete party again, while negative ability checks invert only after the loop.
- Observable Castle behavior: a controlled synthetic fixture with three distinct characters showed that all three results changed with the instruction slot instead of the iterated character, while still consuming three draws. It also confirmed the inconsistent double inversion. The runtime fixture record is `tests/fixtures/oracle/scenario-character-check-indexing-correction.json`, SHA-256 `51c025afb0c18360d911fdffdccc1edcf459046a3f1899e0bf69eada94889340`. The same fixture established that opcode 31 attribute index 10 prompts, consumes one draw, and continues without either XAP; Realmz Rebuilt preserves that separate inert behavior.
- Player-facing problem: an authored “set picked on check” operation can select or reject everyone according to an unrelated party member, and its negative meaning changes depending on whether the author selected an attribute or ability.
- Chosen 2.0 behavior: test every candidate's own value in party order, preserve one RNG draw per candidate, and apply a negative check index once as select-on-failure. Opcode 31's observed undefined attribute index remains source-conformant and does not share this correction.
- Tests: `test_scenario_vm.gd::_test_public_character_checks` covers distinct per-character attribute and ability results, one inversion, opcode 31 index-10 picker/RNG/no-branch behavior, serialization, and forged-response rejection. The differential case is `scenario.character-check-indexing`.
- Legacy quirk: none. Action-slot aliasing and asymmetric double inversion are implementation defects, not meaningful authored behavior.

title: Browser search
text:
## Browser search

Search accepts normal words, quoted phrases, and filters:

- `kind:function` — entity kind such as `module`, `file`, `class`, `function`, `test`, `concept`, `doc-section`, or `dox`.
- `path:src/scenario` — path prefix.
- `module:scenario-vm` — overview/module identifier.
- `dox:src/core` — governing DOX scope.
- `test:scenario` — related test text.
- `flow:save` — related flow text.
- `unknown:true` — unresolved relationships and diagnostics.

Select a result to see source lines, callers, dependencies, tests, documents, DOX constraints, flows, and evidence. Source links use the embedded snapshot and remain usable when the HTML is opened with `file://`.

Selecting a source reference updates the URL hash with the stable entity, path, and line. Those links work with browser back/forward navigation and include a copyable `path:line` reference. Graph node selections stay pinned after the pointer is released; click the graph background to clear them. title: Ownership
text:
# Ownership

- Each route owns a registered scene. Scenes own durable header/layout, scrolling, focus containment, and the persistent Back action for ordinary reversible routes; `ClassicScreenRouter` supplies detached view content and routes that action through the same history path as Escape. Exploration, Combat, and Vault omit the generic action because their spatial or nested return surfaces own navigation explicitly.
- The field Spells route is the persistent-sidebar exception to ordinary inset route geometry: its 420-pixel canonical or 288-pixel Classic scene is deliberately wider than the roster, covers the right edge from the menu to the window bottom, and preserves the map and narrative/footer stage to its left. It suppresses the redundant route heading and owns a fixed bottom context-action strip beside Back so Cast and Make Scroll never enter route scrolling.
- `ClassicPartyRoster` owns the persistent six-slot right rail and Castle's single current-character marker. No ordinary row latches independently: clicking another member moves the marker and changes character-scoped commands, while clicking the already-current member opens that exact Character record. In combat, persistent Auto uses one compact `A` toggle with pressed-state and tooltip/accessibility explanation so all six rows retain an unobscured `HP current/max` summary and the stable party ID is the only mutation identity. A typed `CHARACTER_SELECTION` request switches that rail into Castle's separate countdown picker: the cursor shows picks remaining, portraits receive descending numbers, repeated clicks renumber locally, and the exact count emits one Party-ordered response without opening the Character workspace. The request is mandatory under `FD-SCENARIO-002`: the picker exposes no cancel control and Back or Escape leaves the blocking request pending.
- The persistent roster owns one complete inset panel boundary around its title, slots, and scrollbar; it never appears as unframed text floating beside the spatial stage.
- During memorized combat spell selection, `ClassicPartyRoster` temporarily becomes a full-height spellbook rail covering the otherwise inert Party-command footer. It owns only level/spell/power selection and returns the exact request-owned `CastOption`; closing or resolving the interaction restores the current detached party view and ordinary roster depth. One bounded records column contains the dense internally scrolling spell list, compact selected record, and power choices above the fixed action footer, so no detail can extend below the roster. Every detached known combat spell remains present: request-owned legal options supply cast powers, while known spells without an option remain selectable for inspection with an explicit unavailable state and a disabled Cast action. The list reuses the persistent pressed-row selection language from character creation, while the inset record presents the selected character's detached Realmz-owned description, spell-point cost, range, scaled damage, duration, resistance, and saving-throw facts. Its target badge shares the field/selection native inset and preserves only catalog-proven gradient target lettering from the donor plate. The proven original Cast Spell and Abort controls live in a fixed footer outside the spell list's scroll region so both actions remain visible in the canonical 1280x720 composition and the optional 800x600 Classic mode; their tooltips distinguish immediate casting from battlefield aiming without altering the submitted option.

title: Local Contracts
text:
# Local Contracts

- Workspaces are designed for the canonical 1280x720 composition and remain reachable in the optional 800x600 Classic composition through deliberate compact reflow or scrolling. The 4:3 mode keeps a square gameplay viewport. Intermediate sizes are fallback reflows, not additional design targets; route headers stack below the compact threshold, bound descriptions to two lines, and truncate instead of expanding a workspace off-screen.
- Screens present only detached `GameView` facts and explicit action availability.
- Inventory selects one party member and one exact carried item before presenting actions. Trade recipient rows, Cast Identify's source-selected caster/spell identity, and every disabled explanation come from the detached item action view; the workspace cannot expose scenario-owned opcode-36 escrow as a player stash.
- Inventory inspection renders visibly sized exact CICNs plus `ItemView` facts, properties, and restrictions in the full-width lower record while the selected character, fixed action dock, and integrated six-member portrait selector occupy the right command rail. Its square Done action stays locked to the lower-right route edge above scrolling content. Disabled controls expose source-owned reasons. Enabled verbs enter one stable exact-item operation stage with only visible state, charge/load facts, conservative consequence copy, and fixed confirm/cancel; committed events own the result, Identify remains inventory-wide, and Drop retains its core confirmation. Trade expands an item-local portrait recipient list, keeps the exact item and source load visible, and requires a separate Transfer action after selection. Current, resulting, and maximum recipient load come from `ItemTransferTargetView`; presentation never recomputes capacity. It never reconstructs identified or curse-decoy facts from package content.
- Shop interactions show total payable gold, identified stock, player-knowable carried-item names, exact buy/sell offers, and paid identification. They submit stable stock/character/instance identities and render typed disabled reasons; they do not calculate prices, acceptance, equipment legality, or affordability.
- The Party Wealth workspace always exposes ordinary money management after party setup, even when no location service is active. Wide composition separates Party Pool, all six adventurer records, and the selected-character Swap pane; Classic composition condenses selection into Swap. It renders all three denomination transfers without deriving balance, increment, or capacity rules and never pads the page with unavailable hypothetical services.
- Newly mounted route screens begin at the top after keyboard focus is restored; same-route rerenders restore their prior offset only after focus restoration, and scroll state must not leak across workspaces.
- Exploration and Combat share the shell's spatial stage rather than mounting explanatory body cards. Combat controls stay in the bottom interaction region so the actor-centered battlefield and persistent roster remain visible.
- The Character workspace uses `ClassicCharacterSheet` for presentation-owned portrait-backed character and tab selection. Its Overview keeps portrait and tactical identity, Classic stamina/SP/AR/attacks/load, Attributes, Combat profile, Resources and wealth, and current detached conditions in stable regions: three aligned columns at 1280x720 and a readable stacked record at 800x600. Conditions & Saves keeps named current effects and all eight detached saving throws in two aligned wide records and stacks them without clipping in Classic mode. Abilities separates detached special modifiers from special abilities in aligned wide records and stacked compact records; it does not invent icons or categories. Race, Class & Aging compares the two exact authored definitions beside one another in wide mode, stacks them in compact mode, and keeps the five source-backed age bands in a distinct current-band table. Spells separates the exact known-spell records from the five fixed Classic scroll slots, resolves exact CICNs through the shared media chain, and uses an explicit neutral fallback when identity art is unavailable. Appearance keeps package-owned portrait and tactical-icon roles independent, uses large exact previews and role-local Apply actions, aligns both panes at 1280x720, and stacks them at 800x600; application CICNs never substitute for character identity media. Lifetime Record remains one explicit unavailable record until core owns the lifetime combat/magic history required for prestige; it never invents zero totals from transient events. Equipment separates exact equipped instances from the carried pack side by side at 1280x720 and stacks those regions at 800x600; it does not invent named body slots from unresolved Classic item-type values. Party Order is a secondary expandable editor rather than the route's default dominant content.
- The Allies workspace owns a separately backed current-ally list and detail pane. It renders current stamina, spell points, conditions, source identity, and exact CICN media from detached views, with an explicit empty state and no mutation path. It suppresses generic route helper copy, keeps the list and record side by side at 1280x720, and deliberately stacks them at 800x600 rather than compressing fact labels into unreadable columns.
- Party setup and vault revision inspection reuse that same complete sheet. Setup inspection is a full-stage child surface with an explicit Back action; vault inspection retains the selected revision's eligibility reasons and cannot apply appearance changes.
- Its Appearance tab previews package-backed portraits and tactical icons independently. Apply emits the exact character, role, and appearance IDs; Discard resets local state and never publishes to the character vault.
- `PlayerMapPresenter` and `PlayerMapCanvas` consume only detached `PlayerMapView` plus package media. They may render exact PICT/TEXT assets, topology crop cells, markers, note, and current-party marker eligibility, but they never acquire a map, query mutable topology, or answer simulation questions. The Maps/Notes selector preserves source slots and disables unavailable entries instead of hiding them.

# Scenario VM evidence

title: Castle source/control-flow
text:
## Castle source/control-flow

Pinned oracle: Realmz Castle commit `491816ad60037394f92c428e99c004494d3c28b3`.

- `src/realmz_orig/main.c:46-48` declares a 20-entry stack counter, its index, and the GOSUB flag. This is the source basis for the Classic frame limit; it is not reused as global state.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:97-120` treats negative codes other than -14 and -23 as their positive operation with GOSUB intent. CODE 111 restores the saved action record and resumes at the following slot; CODE 112 drops a stack entry without returning through it.
- `src/realmz_orig/stack.c:3-20` stores the complete door/action record with its slot and restores both on pop. The 2.0 VM therefore serializes the caller program and cursor, not only a target ID.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1573-1632` loads a Simple Encounter, receives one of four responses, copies that response's eight code/ID pairs into the active action record, and restarts execution. The 2.0 compiler linearizes each result as a normal referenced program while retaining the same response-to-result routing.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1594,1661,1692,3734-3737` loads each Simple or Complex `maxtimes` into transient `enctry`, executes one selected result, and reopens the same encounter while the postdecremented count remains above one. Cancellation exits immediately. On the last selection of a multi-selection Complex Encounter, fallback result four is changed to timeout result three. Realmz 2.0 therefore persists the current selection attempt in the typed VM boundary, runs each result as a child program while another selection remains, and does not misinterpret `maxtimes` as a cross-visit usage quota.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:2747-2752` implements opcode 39 by loading the referenced extended door record, resetting the slot, and restarting. The 2.0 instruction replaces the current Classic program with the referenced XAP program; a prior negative call frame remains available for CODE 111.
- `src/realmz_orig/flashrange-loaddoor.c:43-59` loads XAP actions while copying the current AP's level, coordinate, chance, and identity fields back onto the temporary record. The 2.0 VM therefore carries origin context across opcode 39 and directive-based XAP transfers instead of replacing the frame with contextless code.
- `src/realmz_orig/textbox-time.c` sends an eligible timed record's `door` field to `newland(0L,0L,1,door,0)`. `newland.c` mode 1 calls `loaddoor2`, and `flashrange-loaddoor.c` reads that identity from Data ED3. Timed encounters therefore start an XAP program directly; they do not select, disable, relocate through, or destination-recheck a placed AP record.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1736-1815` implements opcode 7 by copying a referenced XAP program over a Simple/Complex result or AP slot, while lines 1817-1823 implement opcode 8 by replacing the active AP record and restarting at slot zero. The 2.0 runtime preserves immutable package programs and stores an equivalent source-to-target program mapping or explicit active-frame redirect in `GameState`.
- `src/realmz_orig/killbody.c:87-127` saves the current action/E-code context, runs or queues a monster's `todoondeath` macro with that combatant's identity, restores the caller context, and removes the monster from the hostile side. The 2.0 equivalent uses a nested serializable VM frame and does not let combat finalize first.
- `src/realmz_orig/getup.c:71-82` invokes a negative battle macro after a completed round. The runtime keeps battle-round macros separate from monster-death macros, but both use the same typed interaction ABI and whole-session persistence.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1434-1447` sends opcode 1's signed message ID to `textbox`. In `src/realmz_orig/textbox-time.c:6-105`, class `-1` enables a click wait for a positive message index and disables it for a negative index; the click path waits for mouse or keyboard input and erases the textbox before returning. The 2.0 VM therefore yields a serializable `acknowledge` interaction for positive opcode 1 messages and continues immediately after publishing negative messages.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1530-1535` passes Classic opcode 3's two Extra Code option IDs to `question2`. `src/realmz_orig/question.c:100-134` keeps the standard Yes/No dialog when the first ID is zero; otherwise it reads 25-byte labels from Data OD, falling back to ordinary Data SD2 messages only when Data OD is unavailable. The 2.0 runtime therefore keeps option labels as their own typed content table and never interprets message zero (`Do Not Use`) as a button label.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1535-1569,3729-3737` makes opcode 3's selected mode zero back the party out one overland step and return before the ordinary AP-elimination epilogue. Mode four sets the instruction cursor beyond the eight-slot timeline; it does not mutate an encounter option despite the source comment, and the ordinary epilogue still runs. `src/realmz_orig/moveparty.c:31-35,65-69` confirms that the negative movement is land-only and preserves the party-facing delta. Realmz 2.0 therefore reports these two control-flow outcomes explicitly: the session reverses a post-move land AP before finalization, destination handling, or random checks, while the VM finishes mode four without executing a later slot.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:1826-1828` forwards opcode 9's signed operand to `sound`. `src/realmz_orig/misc.c:1875-1907` rotates through the configured sound channels, looks up the absolute `snd ` ID, plays a positive ID asynchronously, and a negative ID synchronously. The 2.0 runtime preserves the absolute resource ID and sign metadata while the presentation host owns four rotating channels; simulation does not wait on audio.
- `src/realmz_orig/newland.c:351-404` guards opcode 122 with active combat, no live spell execution, enabled fumbles, a committed physical action, and `q[up] < 10`. `getbattleorder.c:24-80` encodes monsters as 10 and above, making the nested monster branch unreachable. Authored Extra Code sound/text occurs only after that outer guard. The 2.0 handler therefore suppresses both media and mutation for a nonphysical or monster-active invocation, then delegates a valid party weapon mutation to `CombatFlow`; it does not inherit Remake's reachable monster path. The exact live-`inspell` fact remains disabled until spell activation owns an equivalent lifecycle boundary.

These observations establish structure and control flow. They do not by themselves prove every edge case of the Castle executable.

Ownership
text:
## Ownership

- Manifest discovery and installed-revision selection.
- ZIP inventory, integrity, canonical JSON, and package-hash verification.
- Strict schema-v3 domain decoding and cross-reference validation.
- Exact Classic media-key validation and resolution.
- Durable installation receipts and the bounded active/candidate package graph cache.

title: Local Contracts
text:
## Local Contracts

- Providence schema v3 is the only accepted package contract: manifest format version 2, document schema version 3, and mirrored schema SHA-256 `6ef382e35335ba91fc72a94c4600633f68255ad30651a4da195e134887e05bdb`.
- Package decoding composes scenario-owned records with the pinned Realmz application library. It never trusts or exposes a campaign copy as the authority for stock Realmz text or media. `classic-application-spell-descriptions.json` is the current exact application-text catalog; its source commit, resource-fork hash, identity count, and runtime shape are deterministic build contracts.
- External packages receive complete integrity, semantic, topology, media, and cross-reference validation before installation. A valid app-owned receipt permits later startup to verify cheap file metadata, the complete compressed-archive SHA-256, and manifest identity without repeating compiler-level semantic validation.
- `PackageRepository` coordinates explicit collaborators. It does not construct domain records, retain unbounded package graphs, or grant external files trusted cache status.
- The graph cache retains at most the active package and one candidate. Promotion and close release obsolete graphs explicitly.
- Validation errors are detached strings/results suitable for readiness UI. No collaborator accesses Nodes, presenters, sessions, or mutable gameplay state.

title: Work Guidance
text:
## Work Guidance

- Keep JSON dictionaries inside archive, codec, and validator collaborators. Return typed package results and content to callers.
- Reject unknown fields, versions, capabilities, duplicate identities, and unresolved references; do not recover through v1/v2 aliases or defaults.
- Test public installation, discovery, receipt, cache, and rejection behavior. Do not test private repository helpers.

title: Verification
text:
## Verification

- `tests/infrastructure/test_package_repository.gd` owns package trust, contract, installation, receipt, and bounded-cache behavior.
- `tests/infrastructure/test_package_install_task.gd` owns worker progress, cancellation, result handoff, and shutdown behavior.
- `tools/verify.ps1` verifies the schema mirror, synthetic fixture provenance, architecture boundaries, and the full typed suite.

text:

- No child AGENTS.md files are currently required.

title: Godot presentation contract

title: src/presentation/AGENTS.md
text: # Godot presentation contract

title: Purpose
text:
## Purpose

Install, discover, decode, validate, cache, and release immutable Providence packages without leaking transport dictionaries into runtime domains.

title: Purpose
text:
## Purpose

Own scenes, controls, screen presenters, topology-derived rendering caches, animation, audio, and accessibility settings.

title: Local Contracts
text:
## Local Contracts

- Presentation never mutates gameplay state directly.
- Top-row `1` through `0` belongs to the active character's ten Classic Fast Spell slots. A plain number displays the binding and Control/Command-number invokes it through the existing typed cast path. During a manual combat activation, holding Alt overlays a compact animated Fast Spell dock along the bottom of the tactical canvas whenever the character has an assignment; only assigned slots appear in 1–0 order, unavailable assignments remain dim with the request-owned reason, and clicking a legal preview or pressing its top-row number invokes the same typed cast/target path before dismissing the dock. Nonautomatic spells reveal the ordinary visible Cast/Cancel targeting controls; `T` selects/cycles supplied combatants or marks the current/default area center, and Space confirms. Releasing Alt, losing focus, playback, or leaving the request removes it. The numeric keypad remains movement, and application route shortcuts use Alt-number only outside combat. Choosing a Fast Spell in its numbered row immediately emits the binding intent, Clear immediately emits removal, and Back only navigates; presentation never edits character state directly.
- Animation completion never advances simulation; only genuine interaction responses resume it. Cosmetic Treasure transfer overlays also never delay presentation of the next already-committed request.
- `CombatPlaybackController` owns the cosmetic boundary between a previous detached battle view, ordered committed combat events, and the final detached view. It retains the previous battlefield through terminal playback, sequences source-positioned sounds and effects once, masks the combat command surface, and releases the already committed final view only after playback settles or the player skips it. A standalone persistent-Auto toggle sound plays without opening another playback mask, allowing the application-owned queued manual-control change to settle before the next activation. Playback camera focus follows the current action actor across actorless sound frames and overrides stale inspection focus. The tactical camera recenters at turn/focus changes and only when an in-progress mover reaches the current viewport edge, rather than recentering the board for every square. Battle-opening and Auto-controlled action sequences retain every ordered frame but use an accelerated presentation cadence; explicit Auto frames carry presentation-only status and identify Escape as the full-party Auto safety hatch, while accelerated entry frames do not masquerade as player-selected Auto. Manual player actions keep their readable cadence, and sound wait metadata remains unchanged. Reduced motion shortens visuals without dropping ordered audio.
- While an interaction is pending, exploration controls remain disabled and the presenter cannot bypass the session response path.
- `InteractionPresenter` consumes `GameView.active_interaction_request()`: a VM-owned pending response wins, while an otherwise active direct-session battle supplies its detached combat command surface. The latter is translated back to typed combat intents by the host and never masquerades as a saved VM wait.
- Every newly presented interaction resets its scroll viewport to the heading and current task after assigning focus. Long interaction components may scroll internally, but they cannot inherit an offset from a previous request or focus a lower action off-screen on entry.
- A pending interaction owns its source-backed workspace: combat always enters Combat, Shop/Temple/Bank enter Services, and scenario/AP interactions return unrelated browsing workspaces to Exploration. Without a pending interaction, deliberate player browsing remains presentation-owned; route selection never affects simulation or battle cleanup.
- Committing Begin Adventure or successfully restoring from its Save & Load workspace is a presentation navigation boundary: `ClassicScreenRouter` discards setup-only Vault/save return state, inspection state, and route history before selecting Exploration. Later active-session refreshes continue to preserve workspaces deliberately opened by the player.
- Full-window structural Controls such as `ClassicApplicationShell` and `ClassicScreenRouter` use `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`; only concrete controls and modal surfaces participate in pointer hit testing. Router workspaces render above the persistent roster/textbox/command regions so scrolling controls remain clickable wherever their rectangles overlap those regions. The root `InteractionPresenter` owns an explicit draw and hit-test boundary above every nested router modal because mandatory session responses must mask, and cannot leak input to, the workspace beneath them. Its dim shield remains immediately behind the presenter across every same-request rerender; changing modal content may never swap the shield above buttons in GUI input order.
- Whenever a mandatory interaction becomes visible, it reclaims final root-sibling order as well as its high draw order. This keeps mouse hit testing aligned with the visual modal boundary even after the battlefield or another presenter was rebuilt later.
- The splash separates a restrained application identity from one anchored startup command stack and reflows vertically only for the optional compact profile. Its identity pane uses Black Chancery consistently, placing `Realmz Rebuilt` above the project-owner-supplied looping Ogg Theora/Vorbis intro video and `Classic Adventures Reconstructed` below it without redundant lineage or principles copy. The video retains its authored stereo audio and exact 832:480 aspect inside the ornamental frame; each application run starts it muted, clicking the video toggles its audio, and the enabled level follows the persisted master-volume setting. Scenario selection then opens one aligned full-stage row of three independently framed panes: a deliberately narrow installed-scenario picker on the left, and equal wider Character Files and six-slot Current Party panes. Headings share one top band, and ordinary empty states rely on disabled actions and empty slots instead of repeating scenario-selection helper paragraphs beneath each heading. Selecting another scenario may replace a party-setup session, but never an active adventure. Continue remains absent until a typed resumable-save identity and availability exist.
- The scenario picker presents one row per campaign. Immutable package revisions are installation details, not separate campaigns; stale incompatible revisions stay out of the ordinary list when a current ready revision exists. Installed rows say ready/opening and do not claim compiler-level validation on every selection. An arbitrary external path is explicitly installed; deterministic seed controls remain developer diagnostics rather than ordinary setup UI.
- Campaign rows are fast manifest/readiness summaries, not claims of full payload integrity. After selection, the narrow pane may add the exact detached campaign title, version, author, restrictions, guidance, and package splash from `CampaignSummaryView` without making discovery decode the content document. While the host installs or opens a package, one fixed backed operation host shows detached phase/progress data, disables competing scenario actions, and exposes cooperative Cancel; presentation never opens archives or constructs content. Terminal failures cannot be retained or classified until the host supplies typed durable failure state.
- TileMap layers, collisions, AStar structures, meshes, minimap textures, and other caches are disposable derivatives of `GameView` facts produced from topology plus overlays.
- The 2D exploration viewport is clipped to its center panel and party-centered with edge clamping. Its camera rectangle never exceeds the detached 25×25 projection and remains centered within larger stages, so movement scrolls map contents inside a fixed viewpor...

title: Ownership
text:
## Ownership

- `.realmz2` ZIP verification and typed domain construction.
- Strict `.r2save` v4 encoding/decoding, validation, backup rotation, and explicit rejection of older envelopes.
- Installed package discovery, current-revision selection, and capability/readiness reporting.

title: Child DOX Index
text:
## Child DOX Index

- `source-intelligence/AGENTS.md` owns deterministic source indexing, artifact generation, validation, catalog, schema, and HTML template contracts.
- `ui-assets/AGENTS.md` owns exact-commit Classic control import, pinned font acquisition, deterministic slate derivation, and asset manifests.

title: Purpose
text:
## Purpose

Own package loading, schema/hash validation, strict save persistence, and external host adapters.

title: Infrastructure adapters contract
text: # Infrastructure adapters contract

title: Local Contracts
text:
## Local Contracts

- No gameplay autoloads, service locators, `GameGlobal`, `NodeAccess`, or string-based dispatch.
- The controller may call only the public `GameSession` operations.
- Interaction UI responses enter through `GameSession.respond`; presenters never resume the VM or mutate state themselves.
- After a successful interaction response, the composition root may compare detached before/after journal counts and request one transient journal indicator only when the committed view gained an entry. A successful host save similarly requests one transient save indicator. These presentation signals do not enter session state, and the host must not imply an autosave when no autosave operation exists.
- A committed `character_publication_requested` event is the only creator-to-vault write boundary. `RealmzApplication` snapshots the already-finalized session character and asks `CharacterVaultRepository` to publish an immutable revision; rejected/declined interactions and ordinary campaign mutations perform no vault write.
- `RealmzApplication` owns the no-scenario Character Files workshop. It loads the pinned Providence-built stock catalog, runs the same typed creator transaction through `CharacterCreationSession`, and publishes the completed detached character directly to the vault. Selecting a scenario continues to use that scenario's `GameSession`, so package-specific Race/Caste definitions and restrictions never leak into the application-wide stock creator.
- Vault listing converts each validated immutable revision into a detached `CharacterVaultRevisionView` against the selected campaign content so setup can inspect eligible and ineligible records without importing or mutating them. Its public fields and `from_record` factory behavior remain unchanged; presentation consumes the view without defining, duplicating, or compatibility-wrapping it.
- Restore constructs and validates a replacement before swapping the active session.
- Main Menu is the player-facing host route over the End Adventure lifecycle and public `GameSession.close` boundary. The host prompt never enters `.r2save`; after confirmation, the session runs End Adventure and then Party Death package hooks, exposes any typed hook interactions, and closes only after both return without revival. Save-and-return starts that chain only after transactional save success, active combat never offers a save, and noncombat gameplay interactions remain modal. A completed close returns to the unloaded application splash; campaign-library browsing alone does not close gameplay.
- Process Quit is a separate host-owned typed confirmation. Menu and window-manager requests share one path after disabling Godot's automatic quit acceptance; an active noncombat session may choose Save and Quit, which releases the modal and opens the existing save-slot workspace before any write or termination, while battle cannot save. Cancel explicitly releases host interaction ownership so Quit can be requested again; cancellation or save failure leaves the process and session untouched. A pending host lifecycle confirmation owns response routing before standalone Character Files creation or session interactions. Quit never runs the scenario Global quit hook.
- Campaign discovery is a responsive manifest-only library operation. Choosing Play starts one cancellable infrastructure worker for full integrity validation and immutable installation; the composition root polls detached progress, joins the worker at its terminal state, and mutates neither media nor session until the validated result is available. Session-start failure leaves the previous media catalog untouched.
- Infrastructure progress and repository records are converted to app-owned detached view models before presentation. Presentation code may not consume infrastructure DTOs directly.
- Named `InputMap` actions are the host input boundary. Land movement binds the complete keypad compass, including 7/9/1/3 diagonals; the host suppresses those diagonals on dungeon maps before creating a typed intent. Camp, Rest, and Heal are separate typed commands; held Rest, Heal, and Area Search cadence is presentation-owned and emits one intent per pulse. The application catches physical mouse release so rerendering the pressed footer button cannot strand a held command. During a manual character activation, physical Alt press/release owns the transient Fast Spell dock and Alt plus top-row `1` through `0` invokes the matching binding through the ordinary combat response; focus loss always releases that presentation state. While battlefield targeting is active, `T` cycles and marks a supplied combatant or marks the current/default area center; Space confirms that visible target through the same typed response as its pointer controls. Back first asks the active typed interaction to cancel its local subtask or emit a declared cancel/back response, then resolves passive modals, contextual drawers, and route history before returning to exploration; pending interactions suppress route and exploration input.
- The composition root owns one `HeldMovementController` shared by keyboard and mouse exploration. It submits one immediate typed single-step movement, requires a 300-millisecond hold before repetition begins, then uses the persisted 25–400 percent cadence without entering `.r2save` or simulation state. It stops the scheduler at every host/session boundary. The same host settings boundary applies the optional traveled-area preview, default-on Auto Note behavior, Classic/readable typography choice, separate effects/music volumes, global music enablement, and twenty playlist modes to presentation only.
- While combat playback is active, the composition root rejects gameplay, route, and interaction input before it can reach the session. Space skips only the presentation transaction. Roster persistent-Auto toggles and the Escape full-Auto abort are the only gameplay exceptions: the host queues each stable character ID and desired boolean; turning one off settles current playback immediately, commits the queued change, and applies it before deciding whether to run the next one-activation Auto transaction. Escape queues Auto-off for every enabled party character and resumes manual control at the next activation boundary. Battlefield target clicks and Back/cancel remain host translations into the presentation-owned target state; only a completed target payload crosses the existing `GameSession.respond` boundary.
- A terminal session step reached during combat playback does not navigate to setup or campaign selection until `PresentationCoordinator` settles the retained battlefield and publishes that exact committed step. Host teardown and navigation therefore happen once, after presentation releases the prior view.
- The application applies window mode and presentation scales, and translates the shell's centered bounded application rectangle to the map, battlefield, dungeon, and interaction presenters, but those settings and coordinates never enter the session or save aggregate.
- The application injects Auto Switch to Melee only into a manual typed combat-move response. The core owns eligibility, source ordering, mutation, and any pending one-move continuation; no application preference object crosses into `GameState`.
- Direct-session battles expose a detached combat request while remaining intent-driven. The composition root translates that request's typed response body into the corresponding combat intent; scenario-owned combat continues through `GameSession.respond`. Both paths preserve the same presentation component and core legality contract.

title: Ownership
text:
## Ownership

- Classic-wide 2D shell and optional topology-derived 3D dungeon presenter.
- Translation of user input to typed intents/responses.
- `InteractionPresenter` is the dedicated Classic interaction layer. It owns modal/request identity and delegates text/choice, selection, encounter, shop, temple, bank, battle, and one-item recovery controls to typed components that emit `InteractionResponse.Body` variants. Combat targeting and presentation-only commands use explicit typed signals rather than a dictionary command bus.
- Consumption of `GameView`, domain events, and interaction requests.
- `ClassicMapPresenter` rendering of one explicitly framed map stage, optional traveled-area preview, and debug facts from detached map/cell views. It does not expose redundant map-level or input-tutorial headings.
- Consumption of detached app-owned view models, including `CharacterVaultRevisionView` from `src/app/view`; presentation does not define, duplicate, or compatibility-wrap those views and does not consume infrastructure records directly.
- `ClassicBattlefieldPresenter` rendering of the actor-centered native tactical viewport from detached battlefield facts and validated package media.
- `DungeonGeometryProjection` and `DungeonMap3DPresenter` derive floor, wall, door, secret, stair, and column geometry from the same detached topology view as 2D.
- `ClassicAudioPresenter` owns playback from the composed Classic media catalog. `ApplicationMediaCatalog` owns versioned built-in media, and `ClassicMediaCatalog` resolves an exact scenario-package override before the application fallback. Both consume the core `MediaSource`/`MediaAsset` contracts and never depend on package repository or archive classes.
- `ClassicAudioPresenter` also owns one independent looping music channel beneath master and music volumes. `ClassicMusicCatalog` validates the eleven-module application-owned stock Ogg bank and resolves the distinct Desert, Swamp, and Snow preference contexts to Outdoor, while `ClassicMusicContext` selects only detached presentation contexts after Begin Adventure; the splash, scenario library, party assembly, and character creation remain silent. Play switches context, Continue retains the current title, and Off stops it; no music state enters simulation or adventure saves. Custom 1–3 remain scenario-first package resources. Indoor cannot be inferred until Providence supplies Castle's separate base-scale fact.
- The splash owns its intro decoder only while visible. Leaving the splash stops playback and clears the uncached `VideoStream`; returning reloads and restarts it. Hidden setup, gameplay, and routed workspaces never retain or draw the intro resource.
- `MusicPlaylistDialog` is a locked responsive modal reachable from the source-visible Music menu and the Audio preference tab. It keeps all twenty Classic slots visible, uses Play/Continue/Off radio choices, exposes current title/global enable/music volume, reserves slots 18–20, and provides an explicit Done action at 1280×720 and 800×600.
- Picture and sound presenters resolve exact Classic resource type/ID pairs and expose developer-only resolution diagnostics with the owning catalog, asset, hash, and decoder outcome. They never search by numeric ID alone.
- `ClassicApplicationShell` is the sole scene-backed application composition. It owns the compact menu, framed map/picture stage boundary, separately framed right roster, bottom narrative/status well, and contextual command deck. Scenario media diagnostics remain developer-only; the visible picture stage never prints package-internal asset IDs. `ClassicScreenRouter` owns route registration, primary-workspace replacement, history, and focus restoration; route-local controllers own workspace construction and local selection/settings state. Neither boundary may mutate `GameSession`.
- The exploration footer spans the full shell as three aligned regions: an expandable Adventure command pane, the fixed-measure narrative/status well, and an expandable Party command pane. Search mode, held Area Search, Torch, Camp, Rest, Heal, the single contextual Shop/Temple/Encounter slot, and Settings belong to Adventure; Money, Items, Spells, and Maps belong to Party. Extra widescreen room grows the command panes rather than the narrative line length. Typed light state remains visible beside location, time, and wealth; fatigue uses Castle's visible cyan gauge over the authoritative 4–135 range while retaining its exact numeric value and tooltip. Camping changes only the Adventure pane to a labelled inset state; the same Camp icon remains visibly pressed and toggles camp off. Ordinary Encounter samples the exact source-proven yin-yang from application PICT 180 and adds its live caption on Rebuilt chrome; it does not reuse the donor bitmap labelled Special. Heal uses one provenance-bound app-owned glyph because Castle's CNTL 172 is a blank standard control rather than an icon resource. Do not expose a generic Service command or Castle's hardcoded developer Speak vocabulary in release UI.
- `UiRouteCatalog` is the single route, label, shortcut, and workspace-scene registry. `ClassicCommandCatalog` is the single command/asset/action/context/availability/focus registry. `UiLayoutProfile` owns only the optional 800x600 Compact and canonical 1280x720 Wide compositions after interface density is applied. Its Fit policy increases interface geometry at larger 16:9 sizes, bounds the application to a centered 16:9 rectangle on ultrawide displays, and leaves the root stone surface visible as pillars. User text scale remains independent, imported bitmap art remains snapped to exact 1× or 2× pixels, and no display mode exposes additional map or battlefield information.
- Context commands share one application-owned modern slate beveled/focus/disabled surface. Physical holds, persistent Camp, and the currently open Party/Preferences workspace use its recessed state; inactive commands remain raised. Every grouped footer command separates a centered native-scale icon stage from one live Black Chancery caption band. Proven donor controls are sampled only for their semantic imagery, with embedded captions and hotkeys excluded; text-led actions do not import word-bearing Castle slabs.
- Search renders the licensed eight-frame Searching effect at five frames per second while active and a static first frame while inactive, after removing only its six legacy neutral-gray matte keys at runtime; exact CICN 128 remains control-state evidence rather than a visible gray-backed button. Torch similarly composes exact frames 146–154 after narrowly keyed matte removal. Both source assets and their recorded hashes remain unchanged.
- `ClassicUiAssetCatalog` owns imported app-control lookup and keeps those controls separate from package media.
- `ClassicTypography` owns one theme-level role map. Classic mode uses the project-owner-approved Pen modernization of Theldrow letters with the exact FONT 1601 advances for body, narrative, menus, and dialogs; the complete utility repertoire comes from the pinned OFL Grenze Gotisch source, while Samuel's remetricked vector and the unscaled Castle bitmap strike remain reference evidence. Castle's Black Chancery supplies ornamental headings and compact command labels, Castle's Inter substitute supplies Geneva-style utility controls, and Chicago remains limited to its narrow source-backed 3D-help role. Readable mode retains the bundled Alegreya family. Typography choice and text scale are presentation settings and never enter the session or save aggregate.
- The integrated setup workspace uses Castle's stored-character-versus-party mental model: reusable Character Files remain visible in the center pane even before a scenario is selected, while the complete party capacity remains visible on the right. Add and drag/drop stay disabled until a scenario owns party eligibility. Click Add plus drag/drop both emit the same stable-ID import intent...
