# Deterministic Realmz core contract

## Purpose

Own the pure Realmz model, fixed Classic rules, topology, game clock, randomness, and complete mutable playthrough state.

## Ownership

- Direct Realmz definitions and mutable playthrough state, including characters, equipment, wealth, conditions, encounters, battles, shops, treasures, spells, monsters, races, castes, and immutable compiled scenario programs.
- Detached party views include current held-over ally instances separately from hostile combatants. Presentation may inspect these facts but cannot mutate ally ownership or infer a Bestiary catalog from current party state.
- Typed intents/events/interactions/views and the core state carried by session snapshots.
- Pure host-facing value contracts shared across adapters and presentation, including immutable media descriptors/read ports and presentation settings. These records never enter `GameSession` or alter Classic rules.
- `RealmzRules`, `RealmzClock`, `RealmzRng`, topology queries, and world overlays.

## Local Contracts

- `ClassicSpellCapabilityCatalog` classifies every application-library spell definition as a stock player spell, application effect, reserved standard slot, or explicit unknown and derives a deterministic mechanical behavior signature from rules fields only. Presentation art and sound identities remain separate from mechanical parity, and a shared signature is an inventory key rather than proof that any legal casting context is implemented.
- All classes are pure `RefCounted` or value-like data. They never extend or retain Nodes.
- Rule modules may retain the smaller rule dependencies they use, but may not strongly retain their owning `RealmzRules` aggregate; core ownership graphs must remain acyclic so headless and host teardown release complete sessions.
- No scenes, autoloads, filesystem/resource APIs, audio, OS services, wall-clock time, or Godot randomness.
- JSON dictionaries stop at validating infrastructure factories. Domain state is typed and does not expose writable backing dictionaries.
- `MediaAsset` is the immutable content descriptor and `MediaSource` is the read-only byte-source port. Presentation may consume only these core contracts; archive/file access remains in infrastructure adapters.
- `PlayerIntent`, `InteractionRequest`, and `InteractionResponse` use closed typed payload families. Request bodies may serialize only at the save/event wire boundary; core, scenario, and presentation behavior consumes their typed variants directly. A field spell, scroll, or charged-item character-selection request carries one strict `SpellTargetContext` with the authoritative caster, spell, selected power, effective SP cost, icon resource identity, and target facts; presentation never reconstructs those values from prompt text. A request may carry a revision-local detached projection solely as a nonserialized performance hint; codecs and restore ignore it, and consumers must reconstruct from authoritative state when it is absent or its identity does not match.
- Core supplies the typed state, RNG, intent, interaction, and view records carried by a detached session snapshot. `src/session` owns the aggregate snapshot; infrastructure alone encodes `.r2save` JSON and filesystem persistence.
- Classic option-label records are immutable typed content distinct from ordinary messages; runtime choice resolution may query them but never mutate their source table.
- Every gameplay mutation is committed synchronously by the `src/session` transaction coordinator.
- Core never imports scenario, session-orchestration, infrastructure, presentation, or app classes.
- `core/scenario` owns only immutable compiled definitions. VM frames, execution, handlers, and runtime coordination remain under `src/scenario` and depend inward on these records.
- Session state owns encounter attempts/type flags, equipment escrow, mutable base-shop quantities, normalized buyback stock, combat, and scenario-program replacement. These are save data, never mutations of installed package definitions.
- Session state owns the selected Classic difficulty and Monster Set from party setup. Difficulty uses Castle's five signed choices; party commitment freezes the source-authored experience multiplier, while money continues to use the saved difficulty multiplier. Monster Set resolves every constructed monster through the package's complete typed replacement catalog. New sessions deliberately reset both choices to Normal instead of preserving Castle's stale process globals.
- Combat state owns the active actor's action, retained target, and next authored monster attack row. Its nonterminal outcome sentinel is the explicit `active` value; an empty outcome is not an active-battle test. Character attack capacity remains a signed integer half-unit field on `CharacterState`; save/resume may not recompute or round either boundary.
- The Auto button owns one deterministic state/RNG checkpoint across its current activation and any immediately following persistent-Auto characters. Nested automatic activations reuse that transaction instead of serializing the complete battlefield again; any failure still restores the whole chain exactly.
- Session state owns non-VM interaction continuations as well as VM continuations. Random-rectangle surprise choices serialize with their owning region and resume only through `GameSession.respond`.
- Party condition slot 5 owns Castle's persistent Search mode. Area Search is a separate held action: each submitted pulse performs the forced-secret scan and four-click clock/random phase before a save-owned continuation performs the outer one-click clock/random phase. Neither presentation nor the command catalog may merge those operations or aggregate the two Castle random checks. The Torch shortcut resolves exact Classic item 805 through the ordinary charged field-item contract, and the contextual Encounter command consumes its ordered random-door draws and continuation through session-owned state.
- Start Game, Party Death, End Adventure, contextual Shop, and contextual Temple execute as package-owned application hooks through the session VM. Their exact hook identity, program, resume operation, service identity, revival result, pending request, and VM frame form one typed save-v4 continuation. Direct scenario Shop and Temple opcodes bypass the contextual service hooks.
- Live age-band changes yield ordered `age_update` requests. Movement clock work suspends a post-clock continuation whose nested resume remains the unstarted post-move operation, so age acknowledgement and any midnight timed scan precede destination AP discovery. Each typed response advances one character before the owning session operation resumes.
- Monster death macros execute before battle resolution. Their combatant identity, VM interaction, and direct-session continuation belong to the save aggregate and resume only through `GameSession.respond`. Monsters killed by one spell enqueue death macros in source target order; combat state owns the queue, original caster, and deferred turn decision, validates the exact completion cursor, and drains every macro before battle outcome or caster advancement.
- Direct session-owned total-party defeat runs the Party Death hook before aggregate release. Opcode 119 revival records a no-reward retreat, publishes one terminal battle return, and releases combat exactly once without closing the session. Scenario-VM-owned battle defeat still requires an explicit suspension/resumption design before this behavior can be claimed for every battle caller; Castle's callers do not all take the same post-revival `booty` path.
- A placed Action Point's Classic header is a post-action map/coordinate destination. A header that points back to the AP's own source cell is a no-op even when the program moved the party; otherwise `GameSession` applies it only after that AP completes, rechecks the destination cell once, and serializes the recheck depth so save/resume cannot repeat or skip it.
- An ordinary placed Action Point becomes disabled after its complete timeline. Classic opcode 24 Keep Codes preserves it; opcode 25 may disable it explicitly. This world-overlay state is serialized across every interaction and save boundary.
- Every gameplay random draw goes through the session-owned `RealmzRng` and is serializable. Production RNG diagnostics retain the newest 4,096 draws; explicit scripted/oracle sources may opt into an unlimited trace. Saves own generator state and draw count, never diagnostic trace history.
- Classic thief actions map their eight authored action slots to character trained abilities 5 through 12. Timed Pick Lock previews a deterministic clone of the session RNG, then commits only the player-selected frame prefix through the real RNG; the request preserves Castle's 30 Hz updates and final static countdown second without saving presentation timer state.
- Each character owns exactly ten Fast Spell bindings. A binding stores one known stable spell ID and valid power, persists inside character state across campaign saves and vault revisions, and invokes the ordinary field/combat cast contracts; shortcut activation may not duplicate cost, target, RNG, or effect rules. `FD-SPELL-003` permits exact-cost activation and commits only after valid targeting instead of reproducing Castle's prepayment and greater-than-or-equal cost defects.
- `RealmzRng` uses the documented QuickDraw 16807/mod-2147483647 state transition and Castle's inclusive scaling; raw scripted values are test-only branch controls.
- Snapshots and restores detach typed state so callers cannot mutate an active session through a prior envelope.
- `GameSession.close` releases the complete aggregate exactly once at an ordinary or active-combat command boundary and publishes only detached campaign identity. Other gameplay interactions remain modal and reject close transactionally. Host confirmation and repository writes remain outside the simulation; a closed session has no save envelope or pending interaction.
- `MapTopology` plus `WorldState` overlays is the only source for simulation map facts; movement, pathfinding, LOS, search, triggers, and views reuse its explicit cells, edges, and features. Providence's validated fixed row-major compact topology is retained immutably and materialized into typed cells only when queried; local Search and LOS visibility use bounded coordinate probes rather than force whole-map expansion.
- Player-authored location notes are mutable `WorldState` records, separate from immutable acquired-player-map definitions and scenario-authored journal discovery. They preserve independent land/dungeon record streams, stable source ordinals, map level/location, native location ID, and Castle's saved darkness value. Only the party's current validated topology cell may be changed. `FD-MAPS-001` rejects a 502nd record per stream rather than reproducing Castle's append-beyond-search defect; editing consumes no clock or RNG.
- Authored-journal discovery is mutable `GameState`, not copied narrative text or a chronological event log. It stores unique Data SD2 message IDs 0 through 2,999, detaches their immutable package text in numeric source order, consumes no clock or RNG, and validates every identity against content before restore. `FD-MAPS-002` rejects Castle's unsafe 5,999 cursor range rather than indexing beyond its 3,000 saved flags; browsing position remains presentation-only.
- Acquired player maps are immutable `WorldDefinition` records plus stable acquired IDs in `WorldState`. Detached views expose all twenty menu slots in source order, but attach topology cells, exact media IDs, markers, notes, and current-party eligibility only to acquired records. `FD-MAPS-003` rejects IDs outside zero through nineteen and nonpositive icon sizes before either value can reach Castle's unsafe array/division paths. Viewing remains presentation-owned and consumes no time or RNG.
- Land travel accepts all eight adjacent destination cells, follows diagonal Layout neighbors at map corners, and charges the destination tile's ordinary movement cost. Direct movement, detached availability, and land pathfinding use the same destination probe without corner blocking. Dungeon movement and pathfinding remain cardinal and edge-based.
- A topology cell retains immutable presentation metadata for its base tileset/tile and optional special-land overlay asset. These facts pass through detached views but never become an alternate movement, LOS, or trigger model.
- Immutable `BattleTerrainSetDefinition` catalogs preserve Castle's signed mapstats and exact 3×3 combat builds for battlefield construction. They are map-referenced construction inputs, not a second exploration topology. Battle start generates one session-owned `BattlefieldState` from the current map plus overlays before initiative; terrain, source shifts, actor anchors, positions, and complete footprints serialize with `CombatState`, while `BattlefieldView` is detached presentation data.
- Battlefield setup follows Castle's terrain-decoration, formation, party, ally, authored-slot, monster-construction, dead-position cleanup, and initiative order. It is transactional. `FD-COMBAT-006` requires a complete finite placement search and exact state/RNG rollback when no legal cell or footprint exists; no setup failure may leave speculative draws or partial combat state.
- Random rectangles follow Castle's reverse region order, 1-in-10,000 chance scale, three ordered random-door draws, signed one-shot door state, surprise choice, and battle selection through the session RNG.
- A moved-to coordinate selects only its lowest `classic_record_index` placed Action Point. Disabled or failed selected records do not fall through to another same-cell AP; positive sub-100 chances consume one tagged draw, while percentages below one consume none.
- `GameView` and its map/cell views are detached read models for presentation and never expose mutable simulation objects. `MapView.landlook` preserves the immutable active land-art identity for presentation context selection; it does not imply Castle's separate base-scale fact.
- Detached Race/Caste creation options carry authored descriptions only when the source record provides them, plus concise display facts derived from typed rule fields that current Classic rules actually consume. They never invent prose, friendly meanings for raw arrays, or claim dormant source flags as active modifiers.
- An active direct-session battle with no VM-owned pending interaction projects a revision-local typed `combat_action_request`. `GameView.active_interaction_request()` gives a real pending interaction precedence, so rewards and other mandatory responses replace—not overlap—the battle command deck. The projected combat request is detached UI legality, not save-owned continuation state.
- Save-slot previews are detached read models under `src/core/view`; infrastructure constructs them and presentation may display them without depending on save repository types.
- Combat rules publish detached, non-save-owned presentation facts in ordered domain events: source actor/target coordinates, semantic result kind and amount, automatic-action identity, and exact proven Classic effect resource identities. These facts describe an already committed mutation; they never create a playback continuation or allow animation to advance the turn. Character spell choices are staged by spell and power without enumerating every actor or battlefield center. They expose the exact Data AD mask for preview; the final selected actor or center is range, LOS, mask, and boundary validated once by the authoritative combat probe before mutation.
- `CombatFlow` is the stable combat-rule facade. Lifecycle/turn sequencing, character actions, combat magic, reactions/retreat, and monster automation live in named collaborators sharing one typed `CombatFlowContext`; direct and automatic actors must reach the same rule operations and event ordering through that facade.
- Successful battle setup publishes stock sound 10049 before `battle_started` and any automatically processed opening turns. This is a detached presentation request inside the committed event sequence, not an audio service dependency.
- Detached item/spell/monster views carry exact content icon IDs and resource types. Item views retain player-visible item type and icon while revealing identified names, descriptions, definition identity, and values only after simulation marks the instance identified.
- `SpellView` carries Castle-visible immutable spell-record facts needed by the spellbook: level identity, damage and duration scaling, range, target type/size, resistance and save adjustments, rotation, exact media identity, and Castle's exact eight-frame resolution-effect resource sequence. Draft `CharacterSpellOptionView` records carry the same sequence for creation previews; neither view exposes mutable spell definitions or grants casting legality, and action availability remains separately source-probed.
- Each detached carried-item view owns source-probed Equip, Unequip, Use, Identify, Split, Join, Drop, and exact Trade-target availability. Every Trade target also carries its current, post-transfer, and maximum load so presentation never recomputes capacity. Ordinary equip/unequip/trade/drop mutation goes through `InventoryRules`; presentation cannot infer slots, race/class admission, hands, quivers, curses, capacity, or load. `FD-INVENTORY-001` permits an equipped ordinary item to transfer as unequipped while blocking Castle's equipped-curse bypass and stale derived bonuses. `FD-INVENTORY-002` preserves Castle's charged-stack Split and Join results while immediately restoring exact derived load, rejecting signed-short overflow, and keeping the selected stable item instance as the Join survivor. Drop uses a save-owned yes/no continuation naming the exact character and item instance. Charged spell-item use validates the exact owner/instance, permission, context, charge, spell, power, and target before mutation; positive charges remove their per-charge load, negative charges remain infinite, and a pending field target selection plus rolled random field power are session/save-owned. Restore rejects a fixed-power continuation that does not match the item's authored power, and request text retains the player-known identified or unidentified item name. Combat item use spends Castle's movement/half-attack resources but no spell points. Paid identification is available through an active shop continuation; inventory Cast Identify selects the first party-order caster who knows special 48, can cast, and has at least 25 spell points, then spends exactly 25 and identifies every item carried by the selected character. Door/XAP items, scroll transfer/discard, random-power combat staging, spatial/repeated combat item targets, and unsupported passive effects stay disabled until their own source-backed implementations or fidelity decisions exist.
- `EconomyRules` owns Classic shop buy and sale valuation. Sale integer-halves absolute cost, applies charge condition, caps sale inflation at 100 percent, and applies the unidentified one-fiftieth penalty. `FD-ECONOMY-001` treats a zero-authored-charge item as full condition instead of reproducing Castle's undefined zero-divided-by-zero conversion.
- `EconomyRules` also owns ordinary Pool, Share, and Swap probes and mutations. Pool removes all personal denomination load; Share processes jewelry, gems, then gold in party order; Swap moves exactly five gold or one gem or jewelry per action. Bank-backed Swap imports every banked denomination once on entry, leaves the pool untouched on Done, and returns the complete remainder to the bank when movement clears location services. Without a bank, a valid movement attempt with pooled wealth owns a typed saveable direction/choice continuation before passability: decline clears the pool, while accept opens Swap and Done clears the remainder; both resume that ordinary movement exactly once. Castle's distinct internal fallback return is not the ordinary caller contract. Bank-backed shops and temples import and return the same complete pool at their source exit boundary. Every committed wealth distribution recalculates Classic movement. `FD-ECONOMY-003` requires the complete denomination weight to fit instead of reproducing Share's jewelry-overload defect.
- `TempleRules` owns the nine fixed temple services and their signed percentage costs. Temple payment and Pool/Share mutation remain session-owned through `EconomyRules`; presentation receives prices, status, and exact availability but never applies healing, conditions, equipment, abilities, or wealth.
- Personal carried load is a derived invariant: gold plus gems plus fifteen times jewelry plus every item's base and charge weight from immutable package definitions. Character finalization materializes identified starting items with authored charges in caste order, tries ordinary Classic equipment admission, and retains only records that pass capacity. Every item-instance ID has one exact owner across character inventories, party storage, equipment escrow, and combat fumble custody. Vault import rejects an incoming ownership collision before mutation; save restore enforces the same aggregate invariant even outside combat. Vault import recomputes the total against the target package; save restore rejects unknown item identities or a mismatched total transactionally.
- Opcode 36 equipment escrow is scenario-owned party state, not a player storage service. Do not expose `PartyState` escrow or interim-find storage as an ordinary inventory destination.
- `GameView` reports action availability as `enabled` plus an explicit reason. Presenters cannot infer availability from the existence of a control. Combat Move availability derives from enabled detached `CombatView` movement probes while outcome is `active`; a fresh activation with no active turn transaction probes and displays the character's maximum movement even if committed state retains the prior remainder. The same active boundary suppresses exploration Move/Search and field item/spell actions.
- `MapView` carries a bounded 25×25 party-local cell projection, the complete visited-coordinate set needed by the minimap, and movement availability computed through the same topology query as movement: eight directions on land and four in dungeons. It does not duplicate the full 90×90 map for every presentation revision.
- Classic-visible Realmz behavior is the fixed ruleset. Fidelity corrections require a documented decision and source/oracle tests.
- Campaign display metadata, restriction summaries, race/caste eligibility, and character-creation drafts are detached read models. They may explain a legal choice, but only `GameSession` and fixed Classic rules decide whether a character can enter a party.
- Character appearance definitions are immutable package content with distinct portrait and combat-icon roles. Creation and vault import validate stable IDs against those roles; `FD-CHARACTER-002` aliases Human set zero to portrait 257/tactical 9000 rather than exposing missing source-formula resources.
- Party setup begins empty and remains session-owned across any number of finalized-character, vault-import, removal, save, and restore boundaries. Exploration intents fail until explicit Begin commits a nonempty party; no placeholder character or view-revision shortcut may stand in for that state.
- Active Party Order is one synchronous `PartyState` permutation of every current stable character ID exactly once. It preserves the existing character objects, consumes no RNG or clock time, and persists through the aggregate character array. Setup, solo-party, pending-interaction, and combat requests remain unavailable; malformed permutations are transactional failures. `FD-CHARACTER-003` makes cancellation presentation-owned instead of reproducing Castle's apparent cleared-track out-of-bounds write.
- Character generation commits one session-owned provisional `CharacterState` after the complete creation RNG sequence. Review, reroll, cancel, starting-spell edits, unspent-point confirmation, final acceptance, and vault-publication confirmation all preserve that boundary; accepting a reviewed character never rolls it again. The provisional state has no starting inventory; final acceptance grants identified, authored-charge caste items after spell selection and derives personal load, matching `CharacterGen`'s `addinitialitems` order without reproducing its premature `numitems` increment.
- `CharacterCreationSession` is the pure application-workshop adapter around the same `GameSession` creation transaction. It admits only creator intents, uses the app's stock content and RNG seed, and exposes one detached completed character for host publication; it cannot assemble a party, begin exploration, or create a second rules implementation.
- Starting-spell selection follows Castle's seven costs and only the first twelve `cspells` slots per eligible level. Resource-name slots thirteen through fifteen are not character spells. Unspent points require a typed, saveable yes/no confirmation.
- Advanced creation accepts only Castle's fixed `Startlevel` choices through the campaign maximum. It constructs the level-one base, applies the target-minus-one prestige penalty and caste victory threshold, then invokes the ordinary level-up path once for every additional level before spells and initial items. Every registration, combat-stat, condition, spell-point, stamina, resistance, and ability draw remains in the session RNG trace.
- Character creation initializes all forty condition slots from the race, then applies only caste condition-level `1` as permanent `-1`; larger caste values are level-up thresholds. When reached, a threshold replaces a nonnegative current value with permanent `-1`; only an already-negative sentinel decrements. Initial saves use the serialized race/caste bonuses and the `CharacterState` `-99…120` bounds.
- `CharacterState.specials` owns twelve racial combat modifiers. Its separate fifteen-slot trained-ability array uses fourteen authored race/caste inputs; `FD-CHARACTER-001` keeps the unauthored final slot zero and draw-free. Two-hand is retained as a source-owned character statistic but has no inferred combat effect.
- Character creation preserves Castle's complete random sequence: six assigned attribute rolls plus the seventh discarded loop roll, gender adjustment, cumulative race aging rows through the caste minimum age group, final race/caste bounds, three threshold-based special bonuses, stamina, age, and optional spell points. Aging table columns 8 through 14 adjust only saves 0 through 6 during creation.
- Character inspection is detached and mutation-free. `CharacterView` owns named display projections for conditions, saves, special modifiers, abilities, race/caste traits, and all five aging rows; an active row is derived from age without reproducing Castle's view-time `currentagegroup` write under `FD-CHARACTER-004`. Lifetime prestige remains unavailable until every source counter has explicit state and mutation ownership.
- `CharacterState` persists exact age days and the independent current age group. Each crossed midnight and each source-backed age-changing spell invokes one Castle age operation: it may apply or erase only one adjacent row, does not reuse creation bounds, floors maximum movement at two, and adjusts only saves 0 through 6. Maximum age reduces battle experience to Castle's truncated two-thirds share; `doesNotDie` remains stored content but has no invented death or exemption behavior.
- A party-target monster attack with Classic special 17 consumes the generic special-potency draw after ordinary damage, tests save slot seven, and on failure applies the attack-row lifespan formula through the same one-transition aging rule. A changed band pauses combat at a session-owned age update before the next actor; the combat continuation, interaction, character mutation, pending weapon condition, Dragon Hide feedback, damage, and RNG boundary all survive save/restore and resume once in source order.
- Monster status specials 1 through 7 and 16 consume generic potency before their source-family save and mutate the exact Classic condition slot. A negative duration is permanent. Party targets add once only when the starting duration is below 30; monster targets stack without that gate. A monster target above 100 runtime magic resistance converts the complete special attack to a miss after potency and before its save. Special and source-sound events precede ordinary damage feedback.
- Monster resource specials 8 and 9 consume the same generic potency draw before their source-family branch. Spell drain tests save six, transfers up to three points per attacker hit die, and permits the attacker balance to exceed its maximum; experience drain tests save five, subtracts twenty times attacker maximum stamina from direct earned experience, and has no monster-target case. Both mutations and above-maximum monster spell energy remain session-owned and saveable.
- A source-shaped combat spell special 57 uses ordinary actor targeting, reflection, and resistance before healing. Party healing observes stone/death exclusions and caps at maximum health. Monster `cannot == 4` selects same-allegiance actors including self; monster healing retains signed-16 arithmetic, may leave current health above maximum, and marks that monster attacked. Restore validates signed bounds but may not reject this source-valid over-maximum state.
- Monster charm is battle allegiance, not a generic condition: save zero includes party charm resistance; affected party actors are session-owned automatic combatants, target only the opposite side, remain valid hostile targets for loyal actors, participate in outcome checks, survive mid-battle restore, and return to base allegiance at battle cleanup.
- Monster construction copies all forty immutable Data MD starting conditions into session-owned state before combat. Negative permanent values remain active; no constructor may synthesize or discard authored condition slots.
- Monster elemental specials 11 through 15 retain the generic potency draw followed by elemental damage, source-family save, and matching protection. `FD-COMBAT-001` consistently applies protection to committed monster-target damage instead of preserving Castle's cold-through-mental display-only ordering defect.
- Character melee resolves from a validated snapshot of equipped immutable definitions. Armed state comes only from an equipped Classic type-2 item, never from a nonzero damage bonus; conflicting melee slots fail explicitly. `FD-COMBAT-002` makes weapon elemental damage use the defender's save while retaining Castle's immunity, protection, and RNG order. Monster `requiredWeapon` and `magicToHit` are independent attack gates; battle `distance` is placement-only. `FD-COMBAT-003` normalizes specific signed-byte requirements to Divinity Item Numbers and disallows Castle's unarmed family-restriction bypass.
- Ordinary monster melee receives a detached attack context containing the resolved carried weapon, Realmz day, effective defender luck/armor, and party Dragon Hide state. Its bounded fumble-disabled resolver preserves Castle's luck-before-hit and weapon/unarmed damage order, evil-conditional protection, ten-percent floor, typed weapon gates, and Dragon Hide's physical-only reduction plus synchronous sound 694. `FD-COMBAT-004` floors negative physical damage at zero instead of allowing Castle's subtraction to heal the defender. `FD-COMBAT-010` replaces a projectile weapon from the actual attacker's native slot zero instead of Castle's stale global monster; reflection remains unavailable. Castle's positive `behind` is a withdrawal-attack modifier, not character/monster icon facing.
- Battle state owns a bounded twenty-entry queue of exact fumbled `ItemInstance` values and the active turn's committed-physical-action fact. Character attacks consume the level-scaled fumble draw even while unarmed; cursed weapons and a full queue suppress the fumble without changing the attack result. Armed monsters consume the HD-scaled draw, clear only their active weapon on a fumble, and continue later authored rows unarmed. After body-count selection, exact fumbled instances lead the ordinary reward queue and are identified there; `FD-COMBAT-005` preserves remaining charges. The fixed runtime currently uses Castle's default enabled behavior; do not add an `allowfumble` toggle without also source-owning its five-percent XP coupling.
- `ClassicRewardState` owns one bounded ordinary reward transaction: origin, source identity, exact pending instances, pooled experience and recipient awards, detection/identification knowledge, completion confirmation, level cursor/result, and spell-selection cursor. It must round-trip canonical JSON without accepting fractional integer fields. Battle state separately owns exact-once `rewards_started` and `rewards_completed` facts; package validation must finish before either reward RNG or that one-shot ownership advances.
- Treasure capacity uses the exact current `ItemInstance` weight and permits a result equal to maximum load under `FD-ECONOMY-002`. Presentation receives the core-owned availability/reason and may not recreate Castle's inconsistent base-weight strict-less-than check.
- Player-controlled character melee activations normalize any positive prior reserve to one half-unit, clear a negative reserve, add normal attacks plus attack bonus, add Castle's four Speedy half-units, and spend two units plus three movement per attempt. A reserve of at least two retains the active actor. Monster physical activations choose once, retain a living target, and execute each validated authored row in order. Charmed-character cadence, spell/item limits, monster Speedy overflow, and Castle's contradictory zero/one-unit display remain unresolved rather than sharing this bounded rule implicitly.
- Battle state owns each party character's Castle melee/missile toggle. Setup prefers an equipped type-2 weapon, otherwise type 15; switching costs no attacks, movement, turn, or RNG and returning to melee permits hand-to-hand. Equipment projection rejects duplicate type-2/type-10/type-15 slots. Missile mode cannot enter the melee resolver.
- Ordinary physical class-nine projectiles use integer-truncated Euclidean anchor range, the battlefield LOS query, projectile-shield immunity, missile dodge, one damage roll reused across fixed repeated hits, and one player caste-bonus draw. A committed player Fire spends one finite charge, two half-attacks, and twelve movement; a monster uses exact native slot one, retains initial range power while lowering unaffordable cost power, resolves at power one, spends all movement, clears Guard, and targets an opposed party character. Out-of-range or zero-affordable-power missiles continue into the source-ordered cast/movement decision without repeating the missile roll. Random-power, elemental, special, charmed-character, and allied-monster projectile paths remain explicit unavailable boundaries. Monster spell definitions preserve ten native positions; only a wholly empty legacy package array may normalize to ten empty slots, while any one-to-nine-entry array remains invalid because it can change slot selection and RNG.
- Ordinary memorized combat spells cover combat-enabled, non-projectile damage spells without specials. Player admission uses one mutation-free probe shared by the detached picker and execution, including Castle's flags, conditions, round-hit state, per-activation limit, known spell, cost, tier, range, and LOS. Monster spell resolution retains exact fixed slots, multiple magical attacks, Guard/movement clearing, and one persisted post-movement retry; deliberate AI scoring chooses the legal spell, affordable power, and target instead of Castle's random slot/power/native-gap sampling. Failed charm saves continue through Castle's later defenses. Friendly/charmed-monster, class-nine, special, item/fast/random-power, zero-damage, and anomalous nonpositive-cost branches remain explicit.
- Ordinary player automatic-group spells support target types 9, 10, and 12. They select living positioned party slots before monster slots, spend cost and action resources once, roll duration/base damage once, apply defenses per target, and enqueue defeated monster macros in that order. Monster group casting remains disabled because Castle bypasses current power/resource setup; target type 11 is not folded into this contract.
- Ordinary player spatial spells support target types 3 and 4. `SpellAreaRules` owns the eighteen source-ordered Data AD masks; fixed areas use the authored size and power areas use cast power. One typed battlefield center is range/LOS checked, intersecting footprints are deduplicated, over-100 monster resistance is removed during targeting, and party slots resolve before monster slots under one cost/duration/base-damage transaction. A mask that crosses the validated 90x90 field is rejected instead of reproducing Castle's unsafe indexing. Target type 0 remains a separate repeated-selection transaction. Reflection, authored adjacent-mask rotation, and queued persistent fields remain explicitly unavailable; both player and monster paths must reject queued fields rather than silently omit them.
- Ordinary size-zero target type 0 is an ordered repeated-selection transaction. A player chooses one through power distinct positioned actors, including self or either allegiance, pays once at chosen power, and rerolls duration/base damage for each selection. Monster AI deterministically selects up to the scored affordable power from legal opposed actors, while the common resolution still pays that chosen power and resolves each selected actor independently. For ordinary target types zero and one, each originally selected reflector consumes one 33-percent draw before duration/damage, redirects once to the active caster, and retains both selected and effective target identity. An unreflected over-100 monster consumes that repeated selection's pre-resolution rolls but receives no effect. A monster killed by its own reflected cast retains its battlefield anchor, completes the authored magic-attack count, then enters the serialized death-macro continuation. Castle's record-based queue may contain the same dead caster more than once; occupancy remains until that subject's final queued record completes, and the queue is bounded to Castle's 100 records. Nonzero-size open-space placement remains explicit; `FD-COMBAT-011` remains the historical correction record for Castle's leaked local retry counter.
- `BattlefieldRules` is the single owner for tactical footprint adjacency, deterministic LOS, projectile range/target legality, one-step legality, and deterministic pursuit routing. Party movement accepts eight directions, validates the complete destination footprint, and never mutates turn resources on rejection. Pursuit routing uses a deterministic target-goal grid and bounded A* search with one precomputed occupancy map; it respects current occupancy for the immediate step and treats later actor cells as temporary while retaining terrain walls, footprints, and movement costs, so a moving crowd cannot make an existing wall detour appear permanently unreachable or force roster-wide occupant scans for every explored cell. An opposed occupied destination remains an enabled directional command: Guard resolves first, then ordinary melee spends three movement and two half-attack units without moving; open movement instead charges the maximum destination terrain time plus changed axes. A manual missile-mode collision may carry the host's default-on Auto Weapon Switch decision only when the equipped type-15 item has `sp2 > 1100` and resolves to spell class nine plus damage type nine. That one-move decision survives an interrupted Guard continuation, switches to melee or hand-to-hand after Guard, plays sound 141, and performs exactly one ordinary contact attack. Direct attacks and automatic actors never consult the host preference. `CombatState` owns Guard flags plus the source-ordered, serializable pre-move Guard, fixed-origin withdrawal, committed-move, destination-Guard cursor, and living characters who explicitly left battle; interruption by age update, Escape confirmation, or a reviving death macro resumes without replay. Explicit Escape uses integer Euclidean range, Castle's condition/allegiance gates, per-character removal, and the exact 200 prestige penalty. Edge movement prompts or forces Escape before collision gates. Ordinary monsters retain or source-select one visible target, try a direct step, use deterministic pursuit routing, reserve bounded `shift.c` probes for a no-route fallback, resolve party/allied Guard at contact, and attack only after adjacency; RUNS_AWAY monsters instead move away from their retained target, receive withdrawal attacks, and leave at the edge. Physical attacks, reactions, successful ordinary monster missiles, and successful ordinary monster spells clear monster Guard. Fixed-power combat scrolls reuse typed spell targeting and effects without spell-point or spell-attack-limit ownership, charge twelve movement plus two half-attack units after validation, and clear the exact slot only after a successful transaction under `FD-SPELL-002`. `FD-COMBAT-008` removes presentation delay from Castle's 128-sample LOS, `FD-COMBAT-009` bounds its unseen-target scan to validated slots, and `FD-COMBAT-010` makes projectile-to-melee replacement actor-owned. Castle's pre-direction movement-submode Guard check, possessed-character auto-guard, friendly swaps, spell-field collision, target-everybody Guard omission, permanent-Tangle monster movement, and nonordinary spell/projectile branches remain explicit unresolved boundaries. A routed monster without a retained target and a mandatory ally at the edge report narrow unavailable reasons because Castle's corresponding branches are unsafe or internally ineffective.
- `CombatState` owns bleeding recipients and once-per-battle Turn Undead use; `GameState` owns sorted persistent-Auto character IDs. Both are optional backward-compatible fields inside the existing save aggregate. Castle clears Auto when `killbody` removes a defeated character from battle, including the above-minus-ten bleeding range; party removal does the same, and restore rejects stale or nonliving IDs.
- Auto Turn and persistent character Auto share one rules-owned activation routine. A bounded one-turn scorer admits only currently legal actions and assigns positive relative likelihood weights: actual bleeding remains highest-weight; critical healing outweighs Turn Undead, safe multi-target spell value, melee, missile, and movement; moderate healing is lower; spell cost reduces otherwise equal value. The serialized session RNG chooses among the viable action categories, while the exact target, spell/power/placement, and route remain deterministic within the selected category. Forced retreat and single-option turns consume no choice draw, and oversized totals are proportionally normalized to the RNG's bounded range. The scorer never projects future turns. Area damage is eligible only when the resolved footprint contains an enemy and no ally; hard immunity and active reflection exclude a damage target. Area scoring derives candidates from hostile footprints and reuses geometry-equivalent placements across spell powers instead of scanning the complete battlefield. Monster AI uses the same bounded weighted principle for advance/physical contact, authored missile/cast preference, critical healing, legal spell/power, and target choice. Each persistent-Auto transaction commits at most one character activation so the host can yield to presentation and accept manual control before continuing. Auto stops at manual, mandatory, error, or terminal boundaries and rolls state plus RNG back together on a failed bounded activation. Delay is fresh-activation-only; `FD-COMBAT-012` advances a last-slot delay into the next round instead of reproducing Castle's duplicate activation. Manual Bandage exposes one actual living bleeding recipient under `FD-COMBAT-013`; Turn Undead retains source target order, threshold, experience, effect, death-macro, and once-per-battle state. Status-cure spell specials, observed-resistance memory, and persistent hazard fields remain unavailable rather than inferred by the scorer.
- Combat Undo is a narrow activation-start position/cursor contract, not generic rollback. Movement without a result retains it; attacks, spells, item effects, reactions, or turn advancement invalidate it. Save state records only actor, start cell, round, turn index, and availability. `FD-COMBAT-014` rejects an occupied start cell instead of reproducing Castle's unchecked field overwrite. Repeatability and initiative-edge re-entry remain fixture-required.
- `BattlefieldView` may expose the stable active-landlook asset identity needed to render Castle's composited battle art. This is detached presentation metadata only; terrain values, passability, LOS, occupants, targets, and movement legality remain simulation-owned battlefield facts.
- A defeated monster with a death macro retains its battlefield footprint until the nested macro completes. `FD-COMBAT-007` removes the footprint only if the monster remains dead and retains it after CODE 119 revival, so a live combatant can never become unpositioned or make the save aggregate invalid.
- Classic random monster-weapon tables have one rules-owned definition shared by construction and package-readiness validation. Every possible generated item ID must exist in immutable package content; combat never treats an unresolved generated weapon as unarmed.
- Monster blindness and petrification use save seven. Blindness writes permanent `-1` before physical damage; petrification writes Castle's target-specific sentinel, sets health to zero, and skips the already-rolled physical damage through the force-kill result.
- Character vault imports arrive as detached validated state plus provenance. The active session clones the state; it never writes back to the vault implicitly. Finalized new characters may request explicit publication only through a typed, saveable confirmation; acceptance emits a committed host event and never performs repository I/O inside the core.
- Active portrait and tactical-icon changes are separate stable-ID session mutations. Every nonempty role is validated against immutable package content during submission and restore; an explicit empty identity remains empty rather than receiving substituted art. Changes consume no RNG or time and never publish a vault revision implicitly.
- Camp is session-owned exploration mode. Entry/explicit-exit time, service clearing, and persistence follow Castle; the Camp toggle itself never heals. One Rest intent is one source-held pulse: fatigue changes before five scaled time clicks, and the clock owns hourly conditions/fatigue/spell recovery plus half-day health and exact item-877 charge/load consumption. One field Heal intent advances one source pulse, then each party-order type-one/type-two caster who knows special 57, can cast, and retains ten spell points spends ten per eligible wounded, non-stone recipient and restores Rand(8) stamina capped at maximum. Held-over healing remains outside this bounded party implementation. Poison damage and positive-condition decay precede recovery, so Castle's signed Poisoned term offsets the earlier damage rather than granting a net bonus. Land and dungeon movement leave camp through their distinct pre-movement time costs. Timed and random interruption plus battle return persist the owning Rest, Heal, or requested movement exactly once.
- Crossing midnight creates one save-owned post-clock continuation after ordered age acknowledgement. It scans timed records by stable source order, advances a same-day record before chance and requirement gates, persists the scan cursor and RNG, and resumes its AP interaction before later random rectangles. `FD-EXPLORATION-001` guards y with the authored y field and uses semantic attempted/current/committed party coordinates; `FD-EXPLORATION-002` performs half-day recovery once per midnight rather than once per dispatched record. A timed AP may rebase the remaining scan after moving the party. Location-changing AP destination semantics still require their dedicated end-to-end fixture.
- At each genuine field-time hour, party fatigue increases by one within Castle's 4–135 bounds. Every positive party condition decays once, then Torch Lit decays once more when still positive; this preserves the source's distinct `30 * power - 1` light-duration scale. Expiration is a state event, and presentation must rebuild from that state rather than reproduce Castle's stale incremental-redraw edge.
- Providence's ordinary movement cost and blocked-attempt timeclick count are distinct Classic facts, not elapsed minutes. Successful and blocked land attempts apply the five-minute outdoor scale and full hourly rules; nonpositive native cells retain Castle's fixed three-click blocked cost, while an ordinary solid dungeon wall consumes no time. Exact `needboad` values govern boarding, water traversal, solid collisions, and shore attempts. Session-owned boat-presence overlays apply Providence's active-landlook tile-60/tile-147 profiles through `MapTopology.effective_cell_at`, so rendering, LOS, movement, save restoration, and battle terrain share one topology truth. Castle's transient `hitland` counter is intentionally save-owned and bounded to zero through two so a pending third-attempt choice restores deterministically. Special dungeon wall bits and attempted-coordinate timed gates remain explicit fixture work.
- Every character owns five fixed typed scroll slots. Field scribing and use validate exact case, parchment, spell, power, target, cost, and slot before mutation. A rejected or cancelled target cannot spend spell points, parchment, or a scroll. Combat use, invalid-field discard, and case-plus-scroll transfer remain unavailable until independently adjudicated.
- Unsuspended held-over allies are consumed into the combat roster as non-traitors. After combat, surviving friendly monsters with nonzero `canSummon` eligibility return only through the typed Classic body-count selection; negative eligibility is mandatory. Monster targeting compares allegiance, so hostile monsters can attack party characters or friendly monsters and friendly monsters target hostiles.
- A scenario-owned total defeat is a session handoff, not a completed VM operation. The save aggregate owns the advanced issuing frame, caller metadata, combat defeat, exploration continuation, and Party Death hook together. Opcode 119 revival resumes the ordinary caller without rewards and publishes one battle return; unrecovered defeat closes. Special Castle callers whose behavior is not equivalent remain explicitly unavailable.

## Work Guidance

- `ItemView` resolves Castle-visible Describe facts before crossing the session boundary. Unworn cursed records use their native `iscurse` decoy definition for text and statistics while retaining the original icon; wearing reveals the original record. Presentation must not infer this link or receive the hidden original identity through visible fields.
- Prefer small domain modules behind a fixed `RealmzRules` facade; do not add registries or profile selectors.
- Keep character, condition/time, inventory/economy, combat, magic, and monster behavior in their owned rule modules. Opcode handlers adapt Classic records to these rules instead of duplicating formulas.
- Preserve 16-bit and 32-bit arithmetic semantics explicitly where Castle behavior depends on them.
- Keep serialized IDs stable strings and use `StringName` only as an internal lookup optimization.

## Verification

- `tools/verify_architecture.ps1` rejects forbidden host dependencies and direct randomness.
- Core behavior requires headless unit tests and, when source-backed, an evidence-labelled oracle fixture.

## Child DOX Index

- No child AGENTS.md files are currently required; subdirectories remain governed here.

var level: int

var caste_id: String
var portrait_id: String

var archived: bool

static func from_record(record: CharacterVaultRecord, eligibility: CharacterVaultEligibility, current: bool, is_archived: bool, content: RealmzContent = null) -> CharacterVaultRevisionView:
	var result := CharacterVaultRevisionView.new()
	result.character_id = record.character_id
	result.revision_hash = record.revision_hash
	result.name = record.state.name
	result.level = record.state.level
	result.race_id = record.state.race_id
	result.caste_id = record.state.caste_id
	result.portrait_id = record.state.portrait_id
	result.source_campaign_id = record.source_campaign_id
	result.source_package_hash = record.source_package_hash
	result.source_revision = record.source_revision
	result.publication_label = String(record.publication_metadata.get("label", record.publication_metadata.get("name", "")))
	result.is_current = current
	result.archived = is_archived
	result.eligible = eligibility != null and eligibility.eligible
	result.character = CharacterView.new(record.state, content)
	if eligibility == null:
		result.eligibility_reasons.append("Choose a campaign to calculate import eligibility.")
	else:
		result.eligibility_reasons.append_array(eligibility.reasons)
	return result

# ADR 0010: Use one Classic-wide responsive UI system

## Status

Accepted and implemented.

## Context

Classic Realmz is recognizable from composition and pacing, not from stone color alone: map or picture dominance, a six-character roster, a bottom narrative area, context-specific bitmap commands, and compact menus. The superseded dashboard shell used title/route bars, card grids, and a persistent Chronicle column, so it did not reproduce that hierarchy. Realmz 2 still needs responsive desktop layouts, accessible text/focus, and strict detached-view boundaries without maintaining separate Classic and modern skins.

The earlier Remake contains tracked bitmap controls and useful wide-layout evidence, but its host architecture is not a runtime contract. File names alone do not prove Classic provenance or semantic purpose.

## Decision

Use one scene-based Classic-wide presentation system. `ClassicApplicationShell` owns the menu strip, stage boundary, right roster, bottom textbox/status region, and contextual command deck. The canonical/default composition is 1280x720. `UiLayoutProfile` also provides one optional 800x600 Classic 4:3 composition with a square gameplay viewport; intermediate and larger sizes may reflow or scale but are not separately designed targets. Interface density and text scale remain independent. `UiRouteCatalog` owns one scene per route, and named input actions isolate screens from physical bindings.

Import only catalogued bitmap controls from Remake commit `86cf2bf391ef0c43ba31c1633ddd63b7e67e3d61`. Record exact paths, hashes, dimensions, semantic scene-use evidence, and integer scaling rules. Keep original pixels intact and draw interaction states externally. Generated app chrome uses one selected SpriteCook charcoal surface plus deterministic matching frame derivations. Package content media remains separate and resolves by exact type and ID.

Use Alegreya for narrative/headings and Alegreya Sans for dense UI text, bundled under OFL with pinned hashes. Presentation consumes player-knowable detached facts and explicit action availability. Missing facts produce disabled controls or neutral fallbacks, never guesses. Typed interactions retain exact request identity and payload.

## Consequences

- The first-screen silhouette reads as Realmz without a permanent logo.
- Original bitmap lettering does not scale continuously; scalable menus, tooltips, focus rings, and surrounding text provide accessibility.
- The canonical 16:9 composition gets deliberate screen-by-screen design; the optional 4:3 composition prioritizes the square gameplay stage and reachability through compact reflow or scrolling.
- Services and Battle are contextual rather than global tabs.
- Bestiary, Allies, tactical movement, and other unsupported facts remain explicitly unavailable.
- Large text and UI settings reflow and scroll; map/package art remains integer sampled.
- The asset import and slate derivation tools become reproducible build inputs, while rejected visual candidates and dirty reference files remain outside the repository.

func _init(move_direction: Vector2i, result: BattlefieldStepResult, is_retreat: bool = false, is_forced_retreat: bool = false, collision_target_id: String = "", collision_target_name: String = "") -> void:
	direction = move_direction
	destination = result.destination
	attack_target_id = collision_target_id
	attack_target_name = collision_target_name

	retreats_from_battle = is_retreat
	forced_retreat = is_forced_retreat

static func _reason_text(result: BattlefieldStepResult) -> String:
	match result.reason:
		&"":
			return ""
		&"outside_battlefield":
			return "The destination is outside the battlefield."
		&"occupied":
			return "The destination is occupied."
		&"solid_terrain":
			return "The destination terrain is solid."
		&"insufficient_movement":
			return "The step costs %d movement points." % result.movement_cost
		_:
			return "Tactical movement is unavailable: %s." % String(result.reason)

class_name ItemView
extends RefCounted

var instance_id: String
var definition_id: String
var classic_id: int
var name: String
var charges: int
var equipped: bool
var identified: bool
var usable: bool
var weight: int
var description: String
var value: int
var restriction_reason: String = ""
var icon_id: int
var icon_resource_type: String = "cicn"
var item_type: int
var curse_revealed: bool = false
var facts: Array[ItemFactView] = []
var properties: Array[String] = []
var restrictions: Array[String] = []
var actions := InventoryItemActionsView.new()


func _init(instance: ItemInstance, definition: ItemDefinition, presentation_definition: ItemDefinition = null, content: RealmzContent = null) -> void:
	instance_id = instance.id
	charges = instance.charges
	equipped = instance.equipped
	identified = instance.identified
	if definition == null:
		classic_id = 0
		definition_id = ""
		name = "Unknown item"
		description = "Definition unavailable"
		return
	var visible_definition := presentation_definition if presentation_definition != null else definition
	icon_id = definition.visible_icon_id(identified)
	item_type = visible_definition.item_type
	name = visible_definition.name if identified else visible_definition.unidentified_name
	usable = visible_definition.initial_charges > 0
	weight = visible_definition.instance_weight(instance.charges)
	description = visible_definition.description if identified else "This item's properties are unknown until it is identified."
	value = visible_definition.cost if identified else 0
	definition_id = visible_definition.id if identified else ""
	classic_id = visible_definition.classic_id if identified else 0
	curse_revealed = equipped and not definition.cursed_item_id.is_empty()
	_populate_facts(visible_definition)
	_populate_properties(visible_definition, content)
	_populate_restrictions(visible_definition, content)


func _populate_facts(definition: ItemDefinition) -> void:
	facts.append(ItemFactView.new(&"weight", "Weight", str(weight)))
	if definition.hands != 0:
		facts.append(ItemFactView.new(&"hands", "Hands", str(definition.hands)))
	if definition.vs_small != 0:
		facts.append(ItemFactView.new(&"damage-range", "Damage", "%d–%d" % [1 + definition.damage_bonus, definition.damage_bonus + definition.vs_small]))
	if not identified:
		return
	_add_numeric_fact(&"damage-bonus", "Damage bonus", definition.damage_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"strength", "Strength", definition.strength_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"luck", "Luck", definition.luck_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"armor", "Armor", definition.armor_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"movement", "Movement", definition.movement_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"magic-resistance", "Magic resistance", definition.magic_resistance_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"spell-points", "Spell points", definition.spell_point_bonus)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"heat", "Heat damage", definition.heat)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"cold", "Cold damage", definition.cold)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"electric", "Electrical damage", definition.electric)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"undead", "Versus undead", definition.vs_undead)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"demon-devil", "Versus demons/devils", definition.vs_demon_devil)
	_add_numeric_fact(&"evil", "Versus evil", definition.vs_evil)


func _populate_properties(definition: ItemDefinition, content: RealmzContent) -> void:
	if not identified:
		return
	if curse_revealed:
		properties.append("The curse has been revealed; this equipped item cannot be removed normally.")
	if definition.heat + definition.cold + definition.electric + definition.vs_undead + definition.vs_demon_devil + definition.vs_evil != 0:
		properties.append("This weapon does special damage.")
	if definition.item_type < 0 or definition.item_type == 23 or definition.item_type == 25:
		properties.append("This special item belongs to this campaign and does not transfer to another campaign.")
	if definition.special_1 == 120:
		properties.append("This weapon always hits in combat.")
	elif definition.special_1 == 121:
		properties.append("This weapon doubles its magical to-hit bonus without doubling its damage bonus.")
	elif definition.special_1 == 122 and definition.special_2 in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
		var attack_labels: Array[String] = ["one-half", "one", "one and one-half", "two"]
		var attacks: String = attack_labels[definition.special_2 - 1]
		properties.append("Gives the character %s extra attack%s per combat round." % [attacks, "" if definition.special_2 == 2 else "s"])
	if definition.special_2 > 1100:
		var spell := content.spell_by_classic_id(definition.special_2) if content != null else null
		properties.append("Stores the spell %s." % (spell.name if spell != null else "Classic spell %d" % definition.special_2))
	if definition.special_3 < 0:
		properties.append("%+d to hit Classic monster type %d." % [definition.special_5, absi(definition.special_3)])
	elif definition.special_3 > 0 and definition.special_3 < 16:
		properties.append("%+d to %s." % [definition.special_5, _ability_name(definition.special_3)])
	if definition.special_4 > 0 and definition.special_4 < 16:
		properties.append("%+d to %s." % [definition.special_5, _ability_name(definition.special_4)])


func _populate_restrictions(definition: ItemDefinition, content: RealmzContent) -> void:
	if not definition.specific_caste_id.is_empty():
		var caste := content.caste_by_id(definition.specific_caste_id) if content != null else null
		restrictions.append("Usable only by %s." % (caste.name if caste != null else _display_id(definition.specific_caste_id)))
	if not definition.specific_race_id.is_empty():
		var race := content.race_by_id(definition.specific_race_id) if content != null else null
		restrictions.append("Usable only by %s." % (race.name if race != null else _display_id(definition.specific_race_id)))
	if content == null:
		if definition.caste_restrictions != 0:
			restrictions.append("Classic class restrictions apply.")
		if definition.race_restrictions != 0:
			restrictions.append("Classic race restrictions apply.")
		if definition.caste_class_only != 0:
			restrictions.append("Only selected Classic class groups may use this item.")
		if definition.race_class_only != 0:
			restrictions.append("Only selected Classic race groups may use this item.")
		return
	var excluded_castes: Array[String] = []
	var allowed_castes: Array[String] = []
	for caste: CasteDefinition in content.caste_definitions():
		var bit := 1 << (caste.caste_class - 1) if caste.caste_class > 0 else 0
		if bit != 0 and (definition.caste_restrictions & bit) != 0:
			excluded_castes.append(caste.name)
		if bit != 0 and (definition.caste_class_only & bit) != 0:
			allowed_castes.append(caste.name)
	_add_name_restriction("Not usable by", excluded_castes)
	_add_name_restriction("Usable only by", allowed_castes)
	var excluded_races: Array[String] = []
	var allowed_races: Array[String] = []
	for race: RaceDefinition in content.race_definitions():
		if (definition.race_restrictions & race.descriptor_flags) != 0:
			excluded_races.append(race.name)
		if definition.race_class_only != 0 and (definition.race_class_only & race.descriptor_flags) == definition.race_class_only:
			allowed_races.append(race.name)
	_add_name_restriction("Not usable by", excluded_races)
	_add_name_restriction("Usable only by", allowed_races)


func _add_numeric_fact(id: StringName, label: String, amount: int) -> void:
	if amount != 0:
		facts.append(ItemFactView.new(id, label, "%+d" % amount))


func _add_name_restriction(prefix: String, names: Array[String]) -> void:
	if not names.is_empty():
		restrictions.append("%s %s." % [prefix, ", ".join(names)])


static func _ability_name(index: int) -> String:
	return CharacterView.ABILITY_NAMES[index - 1] if index > 0 and index <= CharacterView.ABILITY_NAMES.size() else "Classic ability %d" % index


static func _display_id(value: String) -> String:
	return value.get_file().replace("_", " ").replace("-", " ").capitalize()

		if race != null:

		if caste != null:

class_name CharacterSpellOptionView
extends RefCounted

var id: String
var classic_id: int
var name: String
var description: String
var level: int
var selection_cost: int
var selected: bool
var animation_resource_type: String = "cicn"
var animation_resource_ids: Array[int] = []


func _init(spell: SpellDefinition, cost: int, is_selected: bool) -> void:
	id = spell.id
	classic_id = spell.classic_id
	name = spell.name
	description = spell.description
	level = spell.classic_tier() + 1
	selection_cost = cost
	selected = is_selected
	var first_resource_id := 12_032 if spell.look_end == 0 else 11_992 + spell.look_end * 8

# Infrastructure adapters contract

## Purpose

Own package loading, schema/hash validation, strict save persistence, and external host adapters.

## Ownership

- `.realmz2` ZIP verification and typed domain construction.
- Strict `.r2save` v4 encoding/decoding, validation, backup rotation, and explicit rejection of older envelopes.
- Installed package discovery, current-revision selection, and capability/readiness reporting.

## Local Contracts

- Treat package and save data as untrusted until all structural, hash, reference, limit, topology, and capability checks pass.
- `.r2save` v4 encodes the typed `SessionSnapshot` and every closed protocol variant as `{kind, version, data}`. Unknown kinds, fields, or versions fail before constructing a session; v1 through v3 are incompatible and have no migration path.
- Character vault revisions preserve all ten Fast Spell bindings as character-owned state. Eligibility rejects bindings whose spell identity is absent from the target package, no longer known by the character, or paired with an invalid power; it never silently clears or substitutes a shortcut.
- Discovery reads the ZIP inventory and verifies manifest/schema/capability metadata without hashing payload bytes or constructing every campaign. Importing an external package performs complete file-integrity and typed-content validation once, installs the exact bytes under the package identity, and atomically writes an app-owned receipt containing the schema, campaign/package identities, compressed archive SHA-256, byte count, and modification identity. Selecting an installed package verifies the receipt's cheap metadata and whole-archive SHA-256 before trusting decoded content; it does not repeat compiler-level per-document, media, topology, or cross-reference validation on every Play. Any archive-identity mismatch invalidates the receipt and requires reinstalling the package.
- Long package validation and installation run in a host-owned worker with detached, mutex-protected progress and cooperative cancellation between integrity items. The worker may use infrastructure adapters only; it never accesses Nodes, presenters, or the active session, and shutdown joins it before process exit.
- A package-install worker retains one repository instance across sequential operations so an unchanged immutable package can reuse its typed in-memory result. A fresh process uses the durable install receipt for app-owned immutable packages; absent receipts are upgraded only after one complete validation, and malformed or mismatched receipts fail explicitly.
- Generic package discovery retains every immutable revision for diagnostics. Installed-campaign discovery exposes only the most recently installed valid revision for each campaign, preserves the Providence-authored manifest name for presentation, collapses equivalent rejected revisions, and leaves older content-hash files untouched.
- Validate Classic opcode support, Scenario Action namespaces, caller contexts, typed arguments, Safe bytecode limits, every program/action reference, and the exact nullable Start Game, Party Death, End Adventure, Shop, and Temple application-hook program references before constructing content.
- Providence verifies deterministic ZIP inventory/order, canonical manifest package hash, schema hash, references, topology, and every file hash while compiling. Runtime import independently repeats those checks for an external package once; ordinary installed startup verifies the app-owned receipt, compressed archive SHA-256, and manifest identity before parsing the compiled documents.
- The committed Classic character library is a Providence-built application package with a pinned campaign/package identity and adjacent provenance record. It contains stock Race, Caste, spell, appearance, standard item, and only stock-caste-referenced New Scenario supply defaults; it contains no commercial scenario payload. Release exports include it explicitly. Runtime startup trusts its shipped immutable bytes after matching the pinned manifest identity, while external campaign packages retain the ordinary untrusted import/install path.
- Stock Realmz definitions and text are application content. Campaign package decoding resolves stock identities through Rebuilt's pinned application library and accepts package-owned data only for scenario-authored definitions or proven exact-key overrides. Standard spell descriptions are decoded from Rebuilt's bundled Family Jewels catalog by Classic spell ID; blank campaign fields cannot erase them and campaign packages must not become carriers for the stock description table.
- Runtime JSON dictionaries do not cross into the core; validating factories construct typed immutable content, including explicit topology edges/features, random regions, cross-map transitions, direct Simple/Complex/Thief/Timed Encounters, and rule definitions for races, castes, items, spells, monsters, battles, treasures, and shops.
- Player-map construction validates source order, unique Classic IDs zero through nineteen, positive icon sizes, source-map references, exact signed PICT/TEXT identities, exact CICN 138 party media, ordered marker type-plus-ID pairs, and every opcode 29 reference before content becomes playable. Player maps never become alternate playable topology.
- Packages with reachable battles require complete typed battle-terrain sets. Land sets contain exactly active-landlook tiles 0 through 200 plus global combat tiles 201 through 400; dungeon sets contain exactly global tiles 200 through 400. Every tile has an exact 3×3 build, and every map reference must match its level type and effective landlook.
- Every race definition must carry exactly five signed `ageChanges` rows of fifteen integers plus five age ranges. The loader rejects missing or malformed aging rows before constructing immutable `RaceDefinition` content.
- Placed triggers must carry a valid `postActionLocation`; the loader rejects missing destination maps and coordinates outside the authoritative topology. Unplaced XAP programs carry no destination.
- Standard and scenario spells use Castle's packed spell identity at the package boundary. The loader rejects duplicate packed IDs and unresolved cross-domain references before constructing content.
- A monster using a Classic random-weapon table requires every item that table can produce. Package readiness queries the same rules-owned table used by monster construction and rejects missing generated weapon identities before play.
- Every monster definition carries exactly six native item slots. Empty slots remain empty strings; validation must never compact them because slot zero is the physical fallback and slot one is the projectile weapon.
- Every monster definition carries exactly forty signed-byte starting conditions. The loader rejects missing, packed, or out-of-range arrays before immutable content construction.
- Imported Providence resource-catalog pictures, icons, sounds, Classic special-land `cicn` overlays, every map-referenced tileset, source-backed shared Classic sounds referenced by reachable instructions, and both native facing variants of every reachable monster `cicn` are compiled as content-addressed package media. A runtime-ready managed or scenario asset with the same Classic resource identity replaces the shared-resource fallback.
- Packages with reachable battles require capability `realmz.presentation.battle-atlas-v1` and exactly one valid `classic-battle-tiles-302` 20×20 atlas. Capability and asset presence must agree; presentation combines that shared lower half with the active landlook rather than accepting an ambiguous resource-ID fallback.
- Realmz 2 packages contain one decoded, role-labelled asset for every selectable Classic portrait 257–376 and tactical icon 9000–9119. Missing or wrong-role appearance data fails readiness before typed content construction.
- Presentation media lookup matches the exact four-character resource type plus signed numeric ID. It preserves case and trailing spaces and never falls back to another type merely because the number matches. Package construction rejects duplicate exact keys before presentation receives a catalog.
- Reject a package when a topology cell references a missing tileset or image overlay, when atlas dimensions disagree with its declared tile grid, or when tileset metadata is incomplete. JSON asset records stop at this boundary; the package adapter constructs core `MediaAsset` values and implements the core `MediaSource` port without exposing archive ownership to presentation.
- Save only at committed session boundaries. Save the whole typed aggregate, including VM and session interactions, post-move/random-region continuation, clock, overlays, action state, and RNG state/draw count; debug RNG traces are not persisted.
- Saves may also contain a pending direct-session monster death macro; its battle, combatant, program, VM request, and RNG position validate as one continuation.
- Write a temporary save, read and validate it, rotate one backup, then atomically replace the slot.
- Save browsing enumerates primary and backup records as detached previews. It classifies structural corruption and campaign/package identity mismatches without exposing paths or mutable envelopes; an enabled preview is still fully validated through replacement-session restore before becoming active.
- Restore failure leaves the current session untouched.
- Save installation is temporary-write, typed readback, one-backup rotation, then same-volume rename; never expose a partially parsed envelope.
- Infrastructure may use Godot filesystem APIs; core and scenario code may not.
- The settings repository encodes and decodes the pure core `PresentationSettings` value. Schema 6 persists Castle's default-on Auto Switch to Melee and Rebuilt's default-on Auto Note preferences together with the optional traveled-area preview, exploration cadence, window mode, and interface density, independently from text scale, volume, reduced motion, topology diagnostics, and dungeon-view preference. Schemas 1 through 5 migrate with safe defaults and without gameplay-save ownership.
- Packages requiring `realmz.scenario.gdscript-actions-v1` fail readiness until an OS-confined external host exists. No in-process or token-scanned GDScript fallback is permitted.
- Release exports contain runtime resources plus Godot-generated export metadata only; local MCP configuration, addon code, tests, tools, docs, contract mirrors, and references are excluded.

## Work Guidance

- Keep installed immutable content separate from mutable session state.
- `CharacterVaultRepository` owns immutable `.r2char` revisions under `user://characters/<character-id>/`. Reads are untrusted and typed; publishing uses temporary write/readback, one-backup rotation, and atomic replacement. Archive is the only removal operation. Stable IDs may contain interior dots but every path component rejects traversal names, separators, rooted paths, and nonportable characters.
- Vault enumeration validates each record against both its character directory and revision filename. Current-index changes, archive moves, and exact revision recovery remain host-owned transactional operations; presenters receive detached revision and eligibility views only.
- Character-vault records reject battle-scoped character allegiance. A charmed character may exist only inside an active central combat save and must be restored to its base side before publication.
- Vault records retain the complete detached character, including separate racial combat modifiers, trained abilities, two-hand, inventory, and known spells. Older records missing additive nested fields use the same typed character defaults as save restoration.
- Vault eligibility is calculated against the target package's stable race, caste, level, item, spell, portrait, and combat-icon identities. Missing definitions, wrong media roles, and authored restrictions produce explicit reasons; import never strips or substitutes content.
- Return typed validation errors suitable for readiness/error screens.
- Schema-v3 land maps use `realmz2.compact-cell-rows.v2`. Decode exact Classic boat requirements, blocked-attempt timeclicks, and the active landlook's tile-60/tile-147 replacement profiles once at package construction; reject contradictory flags, land-only facts on dungeon maps, or missing land profiles rather than inventing runtime defaults.

## Verification

- Contract tests cover hash/schema/reference rejection, package mismatch, explicit legacy-save rejection, corrupt saves, and backup recovery.

## Child DOX Index

- `packages/AGENTS.md` owns package-v3 installation, discovery, decoding, validation, receipts, and bounded cache responsibilities.
