# Godot presentation contract

## Purpose

Own scenes, controls, screen presenters, topology-derived rendering caches, animation, audio, and accessibility settings.

## Ownership

- Classic-wide 2D shell and optional topology-derived 3D dungeon presenter.
- Translation of user input to typed intents/responses.
- `InteractionPresenter` is the dedicated Classic interaction layer. It owns modal/request identity and delegates text/choice, selection, encounter, shop, temple, bank, battle, and one-item recovery controls to typed components that emit `InteractionResponse.Body` variants. Combat targeting and presentation-only commands use explicit typed signals rather than a dictionary command bus.
- Consumption of `GameView`, domain events, and interaction requests.
- `ClassicMapPresenter` rendering of one explicitly framed map stage, optional traveled-area preview, and debug facts from detached map/cell views. It does not expose redundant map-level or input-tutorial headings.
- Consumption of detached app-owned view models, including `CharacterVaultRevisionView` from `src/app/view`; presentation does not define, duplicate, or compatibility-wrap those views and does not consume infrastructure records directly.
- `ClassicBattlefieldPresenter` rendering of the actor-centered native tactical viewport from detached battlefield facts and validated package media.
- `DungeonGeometryProjection` and `DungeonMap3DPresenter` derive floor, wall, door, secret, stair, and column geometry from the same detached topology view as 2D.
- `ClassicAudioPresenter` owns playback from the composed Classic media catalog. `ApplicationMediaCatalog` owns versioned built-in media, and `ClassicMediaCatalog` resolves an exact scenario-package override before the application fallback. Both consume the core `MediaSource`/`MediaAsset` contracts and never depend on package repository or archive classes.
- `ClassicAudioPresenter` also owns one independent looping music channel beneath master and music volumes. `ClassicMusicCatalog` validates the eleven-module application-owned stock Ogg bank and resolves the distinct Desert, Swamp, and Snow preference contexts to Outdoor, while `ClassicMusicContext` selects only detached presentation contexts after Begin Adventure; the splash, scenario library, party assembly, and character creation remain silent. Play switches context, Continue retains the current title, and Off stops it; no music state enters simulation or adventure saves. Custom 1–3 remain scenario-first package resources. Indoor cannot be inferred until Providence supplies Castle's separate base-scale fact.
- The splash owns its intro decoder only while visible. Leaving the splash stops playback and clears the uncached `VideoStream`; returning reloads and restarts it. Hidden setup, gameplay, and routed workspaces never retain or draw the intro resource.
- `MusicPlaylistDialog` is a locked responsive modal reachable from the source-visible Music menu and the Audio preference tab. It keeps all twenty Classic slots visible, uses Play/Continue/Off radio choices, exposes current title/global enable/music volume, reserves slots 18–20, and provides an explicit Done action at 1280×720 and 800×600.
- Picture and sound presenters resolve exact Classic resource type/ID pairs and expose developer-only resolution diagnostics with the owning catalog, asset, hash, and decoder outcome. They never search by numeric ID alone.
- `ClassicApplicationShell` is the sole scene-backed application composition. It owns the compact menu, framed map/picture stage boundary, separately framed right roster, bottom narrative/status well, and contextual command deck. Scenario media diagnostics remain developer-only; the visible picture stage never prints package-internal asset IDs. `ClassicScreenRouter` owns route registration, primary-workspace replacement, history, and focus restoration; route-local controllers own workspace construction and local selection/settings state. Neither boundary may mutate `GameSession`.
- The exploration footer spans the full shell as three aligned regions: an expandable Adventure command pane, the fixed-measure narrative/status well, and an expandable Party command pane. Search mode, held Area Search, Torch, Camp, Rest, Heal, the single contextual Shop/Temple/Encounter slot, and Settings belong to Adventure; Money, Items, Spells, and Maps belong to Party. Extra widescreen room grows the command panes rather than the narrative line length. Typed light state remains visible beside location, time, and wealth; fatigue uses Castle's visible cyan gauge over the authoritative 4–135 range while retaining its exact numeric value and tooltip. Camping changes only the Adventure pane to a labelled inset state; the same Camp icon remains visibly pressed and toggles camp off. Ordinary Encounter samples the exact source-proven yin-yang from application PICT 180 and adds its live caption on Rebuilt chrome; it does not reuse the donor bitmap labelled Special. Heal uses one provenance-bound app-owned glyph because Castle's CNTL 172 is a blank standard control rather than an icon resource. Do not expose a generic Service command or Castle's hardcoded developer Speak vocabulary in release UI.
- `UiRouteCatalog` is the single route, label, shortcut, and workspace-scene registry. `ClassicCommandCatalog` is the single command/asset/action/context/availability/focus registry. `UiLayoutProfile` owns only the optional 800x600 Compact and canonical 1280x720 Wide compositions after interface density is applied. Its Fit policy increases interface geometry at larger 16:9 sizes, bounds the application to a centered 16:9 rectangle on ultrawide displays, and leaves the root stone surface visible as pillars. User text scale remains independent, imported bitmap art remains snapped to exact 1× or 2× pixels, and no display mode exposes additional map or battlefield information.
- Context commands share one application-owned modern slate beveled/focus/disabled surface. Physical holds, persistent Camp, and the currently open Party/Preferences workspace use its recessed state; inactive commands remain raised. Every grouped footer command separates a centered native-scale icon stage from one live Black Chancery caption band. Proven donor controls are sampled only for their semantic imagery, with embedded captions and hotkeys excluded; text-led actions do not import word-bearing Castle slabs.
- Search renders the licensed eight-frame Searching effect at five frames per second while active and a static first frame while inactive, after removing only its six legacy neutral-gray matte keys at runtime; exact CICN 128 remains control-state evidence rather than a visible gray-backed button. Torch similarly composes exact frames 146–154 after narrowly keyed matte removal. Both source assets and their recorded hashes remain unchanged.
- `ClassicUiAssetCatalog` owns imported app-control lookup and keeps those controls separate from package media.
- `ClassicTypography` owns one theme-level role map. Classic mode uses the project-owner-approved Pen modernization of Theldrow letters with the exact FONT 1601 advances for body, narrative, menus, and dialogs; the complete utility repertoire comes from the pinned OFL Grenze Gotisch source, while Samuel's remetricked vector and the unscaled Castle bitmap strike remain reference evidence. Castle's Black Chancery supplies ornamental headings and compact command labels, Castle's Inter substitute supplies Geneva-style utility controls, and Chicago remains limited to its narrow source-backed 3D-help role. Readable mode retains the bundled Alegreya family. Typography choice and text scale are presentation settings and never enter the session or save aggregate.
- The integrated setup workspace uses Castle's stored-character-versus-party mental model: reusable Character Files remain visible in the center pane even before a scenario is selected, while the complete party capacity remains visible on the right. Add and drag/drop stay disabled until a scenario owns party eligibility. Click Add plus drag/drop both emit the same stable-ID import intent. Portrait and summary children ignore pointer input so dragging anywhere on a Character Files row reaches its one typed drag source; the complete party list owns the matching drop target and highlights while accepting a drag. Character Files and Current Party use aligned row surfaces and render the exact package-provided 44×44 in-game portrait from `CharacterView.portrait_id` at full size; dragging temporarily replaces every native drag/can-drop/forbidden cursor shape with a translucent copy of that portrait and restores the system cursors when the drag ends. The picker never substitutes a tactical CICN or forces its pixel-art texture filter. The full-width setup surface is opaque so the persistent exploration roster cannot appear underneath it as a second party list. Create Character replaces the entire assembly row with exactly one of the five stages—Identity, Race & Caste, Appearance, Review, or Spells—and returns to assembly after finalization or cancellation; the assembly roster is never shown beside a creator stage. Without a selected scenario it uses the stock application catalog; with a selected scenario it uses that package's standard/custom definitions and restrictions. Race is the left-hand driver; each Race and Caste record pairs one narrow spellbook-style pressed selector with a wider selected-definition pane containing its authored description and named compatibility facts, compatible named Castes sort first, and literal compiler fallback labels such as `Race 2` and `Caste 2` remain absent from ordinary creation. Revision history, restore, and archive remain in the advanced Vault workspace. Appearance labels each six-choice row from explicit race recommendation metadata. Review reuses the complete detached character sheet without a redundant party picker. Spells reuses the ordinary spellbook's level-rail/list/detail hierarchy with normal pressed toggle state, typed costs, readable source descriptions, and the exact detached eight-frame Classic effect sequence. A preview appears only when all eight exact resources resolve and decode to meaningful pixels; incomplete, blank, or unavailable sequences are omitted rather than shown partially or replaced. No modifier-key instruction copy appears. Media choices remain explicit compiled content, never guessed filesystem paths.
- Party setup renders all six current-party slots with full-size portraits and without scrolling at the minimum viewport, removing assembly-only helper copy before shrinking portraits. It presents Monster Set in Normal, Mega, Monster order alongside source-authored recommended/maximum/current aggregate levels and the core-computed experience percentage. Difficulty and Monster Set controls emit one typed setup intent; labels and availability come from the detached `PartySetupView`, and presentation never recomputes reward scaling or monster identity.
- Appearance may sort detached options and decode their package thumbnails, but it retains stable asset IDs and never enumerates host folders. The selected portrait may pair its corresponding tactical icon only until the player explicitly changes that icon.
- Identity exposes Castle's fixed starting levels filtered by the campaign maximum. Its backed Character File preview shows only the entered name, gender, and starting level until Appearance supplies exact package-owned media. Race and Caste remain equal left/right selectors in both supported profiles; authored descriptions are visible, while absent descriptions and unproven emblems remain absent. Review renders exact portrait, tactical-icon, and starting-item identities when resolvable, states missing media explicitly, and stacks its typed records in the compact profile. Presentation submits the selected level and renders the resulting session-owned draft; it never synthesizes an advanced character, restriction, media identity, or progression result. Reroll and acceptance emit typed intents; the unspent-spell and vault-publication confirmations are session-owned interactions, not local dialog shortcuts.
- The Character Files workspace is a full-stage route that suppresses the persistent roster, textbox, and command deck. It renders detached immutable revision history and exact eligibility reasons with the complete viewport available. Archive/recovery signals cross to the host repository; presentation never opens, moves, rewrites, or deletes `.r2char` files.
- Application workspaces normally suppress the exploration/combat roster and use the full viewport. Every ordinary routed workspace owns one persistent visible Back, Done, or Cancel action wired to the same history path as Escape; nested modal or inspection tasks retain their more specific local action. Character and Inventory own compact task-specific member selectors. Inventory follows Castle's working-screen hierarchy: one visibly icon-led carried-item field with detached Damage/Armor line annotations on the left, one selected-character record with fixed item actions and an integrated six-member portrait selector on the right, one full-width selected-item narrative/fact record below, and one square fixed lower-right Done. Trade recipients remain beside the exact selected item and never use a hidden or second inventory list; exact CICNs, identified facts, restrictions, and source-owned availability stay detached, and presentation never infers inventory legality locally. Field Spells is the deliberate Castle-shaped exception: it preserves the live map/picture renderer and left narrative/footer while a 420-pixel canonical or 288-pixel compact persistent sidebar covers the complete right edge, including Party commands. Both profiles retain Castle's vertical level-and-power rail beside dense same-level rows and a bounded one-line selected record; the route omits a redundant page heading and fixes Cast, Make Scroll, and Back outside all scrolling content. Fast Spell bindings and the scroll case may scroll independently when their fixed Classic slot counts require it. Ordinary spell records never display the combat-queue CICN as a spellbook identity icon. Encounter and combat spell selection use the same shared level-filter contract in their roster rectangle. Mandatory party-target selection restores the numbered roster and keeps the committed spell, selected power, effective cost, and target facts visible. Exact Cast/Abort art is shown only for proven identities. Donor-proven target labels retain their original gradient glyph pixels but key away the donor gray plate onto one shared native Rebuilt inset; ambiguous target types remain ordinary semantic facts and do not receive invented badge art.
- The System workspace renders detached primary/backup save previews and exact corruption or identity-mismatch reasons. Browsing never opens save files, and choosing a candidate delegates full validation and replacement-session restore to the host. The splash Load path first selects the owning installed scenario, then opens that package-bound workspace; party setup exposes the same workspace beside Begin Adventure. Back returns to setup, while a successful restore clears setup-only route state and enters the restored play route.
- Finalized and imported setup members render only from `GameView`; Add, Remove, and Begin emit typed intents. The presenter does not retain a parallel party array or infer that a committed setup edit has begun the adventure. Because party setup suppresses the ordinary shell status region, rejected setup intents render their exact core-owned reason inside the assembly surface; the presenter does not recreate duplicate-character or eligibility rules. Setup inspection fills the setup viewport on an opaque clipped surface above assembly, so the complete character sheet never composites with the picker beneath it.
- Party setup and campaign-aware vault browsing reuse `ClassicCharacterSheet` for complete mutation-free inspection before import or Begin. Eligible and ineligible revisions keep their exact target-campaign reasons visible; inspection never changes or republishes a vault revision.
- Cosmetic-only animation and randomness.

## Local Contracts

- Presentation never mutates gameplay state directly.
- Top-row `1` through `0` belongs to the active character's ten Classic Fast Spell slots. A plain number displays the binding and Control/Command-number invokes it through the existing typed cast path. During a manual combat activation, holding Alt overlays a compact animated Fast Spell dock along the bottom of the tactical canvas whenever the character has an assignment; only assigned slots appear in 1–0 order, unavailable assignments remain dim with the request-owned reason, and clicking a legal preview or pressing its top-row number invokes the same typed cast/target path before dismissing the dock. Nonautomatic spells reveal the ordinary visible Cast/Cancel targeting controls; `T` selects/cycles supplied combatants or marks the current/default area center, and Space confirms. Releasing Alt, losing focus, playback, or leaving the request removes it. The numeric keypad remains movement, and application route shortcuts use Alt-number only outside combat. Choosing a Fast Spell in its numbered row immediately emits the binding intent, Clear immediately emits removal, and Back only navigates; presentation never edits character state directly.
- Animation completion never advances simulation; only genuine interaction responses resume it. Cosmetic Treasure transfer overlays also never delay presentation of the next already-committed request.
- `CombatPlaybackController` owns the cosmetic boundary between a previous detached battle view, ordered committed combat events, and the final detached view. It retains the previous battlefield through terminal playback, sequences source-positioned sounds and effects once, masks the combat command surface, and releases the already committed final view only after playback settles or the player skips it. A standalone persistent-Auto toggle sound plays without opening another playback mask, allowing the application-owned queued manual-control change to settle before the next activation. Playback camera focus follows the current action actor across actorless sound frames and overrides stale inspection focus. The tactical camera recenters at turn/focus changes and only when an in-progress mover reaches the current viewport edge, rather than recentering the board for every square. Battle-opening and Auto-controlled action sequences retain every ordered frame but use an accelerated presentation cadence; explicit Auto frames carry presentation-only status and identify Escape as the full-party Auto safety hatch, while accelerated entry frames do not masquerade as player-selected Auto. Manual player actions keep their readable cadence, and sound wait metadata remains unchanged. Reduced motion shortens visuals without dropping ordered audio.
- While an interaction is pending, exploration controls remain disabled and the presenter cannot bypass the session response path.
- `InteractionPresenter` consumes `GameView.active_interaction_request()`: a VM-owned pending response wins, while an otherwise active direct-session battle supplies its detached combat command surface. The latter is translated back to typed combat intents by the host and never masquerades as a saved VM wait.
- Every newly presented interaction resets its scroll viewport to the heading and current task after assigning focus. Long interaction components may scroll internally, but they cannot inherit an offset from a previous request or focus a lower action off-screen on entry.
- A pending interaction owns its source-backed workspace: combat always enters Combat, Shop/Temple/Bank enter Services, and scenario/AP interactions return unrelated browsing workspaces to Exploration. Without a pending interaction, deliberate player browsing remains presentation-owned; route selection never affects simulation or battle cleanup.
- Committing Begin Adventure or successfully restoring from its Save & Load workspace is a presentation navigation boundary: `ClassicScreenRouter` discards setup-only Vault/save return state, inspection state, and route history before selecting Exploration. Later active-session refreshes continue to preserve workspaces deliberately opened by the player.
- Full-window structural Controls such as `ClassicApplicationShell` and `ClassicScreenRouter` use `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`; only concrete controls and modal surfaces participate in pointer hit testing. Router workspaces render above the persistent roster/textbox/command regions so scrolling controls remain clickable wherever their rectangles overlap those regions. The root `InteractionPresenter` owns an explicit draw and hit-test boundary above every nested router modal because mandatory session responses must mask, and cannot leak input to, the workspace beneath them. Its dim shield remains immediately behind the presenter across every same-request rerender; changing modal content may never swap the shield above buttons in GUI input order.
- Whenever a mandatory interaction becomes visible, it reclaims final root-sibling order as well as its high draw order. This keeps mouse hit testing aligned with the visual modal boundary even after the battlefield or another presenter was rebuilt later.
- The splash separates a restrained application identity from one anchored startup command stack and reflows vertically only for the optional compact profile. Its identity pane uses Black Chancery consistently, placing `Realmz Rebuilt` above the project-owner-supplied looping Ogg Theora/Vorbis intro video and `Classic Adventures Reconstructed` below it without redundant lineage or principles copy. The video retains its authored stereo audio and exact 832:480 aspect inside the ornamental frame; each application run starts it muted, clicking the video toggles its audio, and the enabled level follows the persisted master-volume setting. Scenario selection then opens one aligned full-stage row of three independently framed panes: a deliberately narrow installed-scenario picker on the left, and equal wider Character Files and six-slot Current Party panes. Headings share one top band, and ordinary empty states rely on disabled actions and empty slots instead of repeating scenario-selection helper paragraphs beneath each heading. Selecting another scenario may replace a party-setup session, but never an active adventure. Continue remains absent until a typed resumable-save identity and availability exist.
- The scenario picker presents one row per campaign. Immutable package revisions are installation details, not separate campaigns; stale incompatible revisions stay out of the ordinary list when a current ready revision exists. Installed rows say ready/opening and do not claim compiler-level validation on every selection. An arbitrary external path is explicitly installed; deterministic seed controls remain developer diagnostics rather than ordinary setup UI.
- Campaign rows are fast manifest/readiness summaries, not claims of full payload integrity. After selection, the narrow pane may add the exact detached campaign title, version, author, restrictions, guidance, and package splash from `CampaignSummaryView` without making discovery decode the content document. While the host installs or opens a package, one fixed backed operation host shows detached phase/progress data, disables competing scenario actions, and exposes cooperative Cancel; presentation never opens archives or constructs content. Terminal failures cannot be retained or classified until the host supplies typed durable failure state.
- TileMap layers, collisions, AStar structures, meshes, minimap textures, and other caches are disposable derivatives of `GameView` facts produced from topology plus overlays.
- The 2D exploration viewport is clipped to its center panel and party-centered with edge clamping. Its camera rectangle never exceeds the detached 25×25 projection and remains centered within larger stages, so movement scrolls map contents inside a fixed viewport instead of moving that viewport across the shell. Land atlases render at their native 32×32 cell size from each detached cell's `tileset_id` and `render_tile`; a cell's optional Classic special-land image renders above that base tile. Dungeon composition uses the same detached feature and edge facts as the topology views.
- Empty width beside the integer-sized exploration map is application chrome, not dead black space or map truth. It tiles the approved charcoal-slate material and centers the manifest-backed low-contrast exploration rail without stretching it beyond its native production size; the chrome frames rather than scales or extends the map. The six-member roster and canonical Adventure/Party command panes hide their scrollbars whenever their complete fixed content fits.
- Exploration Search renders exact CICN 128 as a persistent toggle. Held Area Search uses the licensed non-commercial Realmz eye/label bitmap from its exact tracked donor commit; exact generic CICN 130/129 released/pressed plates remain cataloged as Castle control-state evidence and are not mislabelled as the visible icon. The custom torch meter renders exact frames 146–153 over segmented body 154 only when the detached party owns Classic item 805, animates only while Light is positive, and shortens from the detached remaining-light value without changing time or inventory.
- Ordinary land travel draws exact built-in Classic CICN 175 when facing west and CICN 186 when facing east, at native 32×32 map-cell size without directional-arrow decoration. Vertical movement preserves the prior horizontal facing. Camp mode draws exact built-in CICN 178 and restores the preserved mounted facing when Camp is toggled off. The abstract yellow ring is permitted only when the selected verified app-owned asset fails to load; boat and base-scale tactical variants require their own proven assets before use.
- Normal play never paints topology grid lines, AP markers, random-rectangle bounds, or abstract land edges over Classic art. Those remain opt-in debug facts. Land click/hold movement uses Castle's independent horizontal/vertical pointer regions for eight directions; dungeon clicks remain cardinal. Both emit typed movement intent only.
- Keyboard and mouse exploration holds share one presentation-owned scheduler. The first press moves immediately; the persisted 25–400 percent setting controls only repeat cadence, never simulation time. The scheduler permits one synchronous movement transaction at a time, never catches up missed intervals, and stops on release, focus loss, route/modal changes, blocked movement, transitions, combat, or scenario interaction.
- Exploration cadence is measured start-to-start: synchronous transaction and presentation work consumes the current interval, and a slow frame emits at most one next step rather than a catch-up burst. Ordinary movement retains the existing command controls and updates availability in place; route, modal, and context changes remain the only reasons to rebuild that deck. Full-stage party setup owns its assembly list and must not rebuild the hidden persistent gameplay roster. Package and application image decoding is shared through the effective media catalog for its lifetime.
- Switching between 2D and 3D changes only presentation settings. It cannot create collision, movement, LOS, discovery, or door state.
- Presentation and accessibility settings cannot change rules.
- Auto Switch to Melee is a persisted application convenience preference, defaulted on from Castle's bundled preferences. Presentation attaches its boolean value only to a manual combat movement response; it never mutates battle weapon mode or supplies the preference to direct Attack, current-turn Auto, persistent Auto, charmed actors, or monsters.
- Realmz Rebuilt has one visual system. Verified base-game command bitmaps and integrated Classic media are application-owned, versioned assets; scenario-owned CICNs, portraits, pictures, sounds, and map art remain package content. Exact scenario `(resource type, ID)` keys override the corresponding application key. Application PICT/CICN families migrate only after their package-reference and readiness contracts are proven; numeric ID alone never selects an owner. Both catalogs use nearest-neighbor sampling where applicable and never share an ambiguous lookup. Slate backgrounds and frame centers use the manifest-backed seamless tile at native scale with repeat enabled; responsive containers crop or tile it and never stretch it. Generated raised/inset bevels retain opaque slate through their complete bounds so buttons and panels never expose accidental parent-colored corner gaps.
- If an action has no verified bitmap in the app-owned catalog, render its ordinary text label through the shared theme. Never construct a blank `TextureButton`, repurpose a status marker as command art, or make hover text the only visible action identity.
- Interface density and text scale are independent. The canonical composition is 1280x720. The optional 800x600 Classic mode uses its own compact 4:3 composition and square gameplay viewport; other window sizes may reflow but are not independently designed or accepted. Controls stack, wrap, or scroll when necessary and never fractionally scale Classic map/content art.
- Unidentified item views expose only player-knowable names and details. Presentation never reveals identified descriptions, values, curse relationships, or other hidden definition facts.
- The ordinary inventory workspace is character-first, then exact-instance-first. It renders the item view's typed action availability and trade recipients and emits stable IDs only; it never reproduces slot, restriction, curse, capacity, load, charge, spell, or targeting rules. Its Cast Identify control carries the core-selected caster, special-48 spell, and target character through the typed spell-intent family; presentation neither chooses eligibility nor identifies only the selected instance. Field item targets use the typed character-selection component; combat item options come entirely from the combat request. It has no player Store command unless a separate source-backed service contract is introduced.
- Screen workspaces live inside clipped vertical scroll surfaces so long inventories, service actions, and accessibility-scaled text remain reachable. Classic textbox interactions reuse the shell's exact narrative well instead of replacing the whole footer: positive source text advances from a click on that surface or Enter, while authored Yes/No and indexed responses occupy one content-width floating pane immediately above the well so the complete well remains available to source text. Encounter, Level Result/Spell Learning, surviving-allies selection, and host lifecycle confirmation use centered locked floating modals over the unchanged application; their presenter-owned dim shield blocks input outside the frame and their explicit actions or Escape-compatible typed cancel/back response own dismissal. Treasure, Shop, Temple, Bank, and pooled-departure distribution remain opaque full application workspaces spanning the play stage and lower command region. Treasure's leave-behind warning is a nested locked modal that retains the current distribution workspace beneath it. There is no persistent Chronicle column.
- Campaign selection and party setup use the already aligned root stone as one full-stage surface. They suppress the map frame, play textbox, and command deck until an active workspace returns, avoiding a second texture origin, structural seams, or overlapping play controls.
- Before campaign selection, the presentation-owned splash is the complete pre-session front door. It offers scenario selection, reusable Character Files, and process Quit without constructing a campaign `GameSession`. The stock Character Files creator is available without a scenario; selecting a scenario switches creation to that package's custom definitions and eligibility context. Scenario installation uses one file picker restricted to `.realmz2`; ordinary players never type a filesystem path. Classic Theldrow uses a 17-pixel default before the user text-scale multiplier; dense records may use smaller explicit sizes only when they remain legible at both supported compositions. Creator identity fields, setup selectors, and creator actions use the same Theldrow family as the surrounding Classic controls.
- Ordinary party assembly shows reusable characters and all six current-party positions directly. At 1280x720 all six party rows and primary actions remain visible together; at 800x600 the active creator owns the full width and the reusable-character list uses bounded pagination rather than pushing actions below the viewport. Revision history, archive operations, and recovery remain optional secondary content in the full-stage Character Files workspace and do not occupy the party-builder footer.
- Menu routes are rebuilt whenever session, overlay, or route ownership changes. No-session, party-setup, mandatory-interaction, and active-combat states expose only commands that are valid in that host state; a disabled child-only menu is itself disabled. Popup and option-menu panels are opaque through their complete border bounds.
- Spatial map and dungeon presenters follow that same play-stage visibility boundary. They remain hidden beneath campaign selection and party setup even when Explore is still the active route.
- A positive Classic message reuses the shell's exact narrative-well bounds at the compact 18-pixel interaction role and advances when the player clicks that text surface or presses Enter/Space; it does not invent a formal Continue button or render generic Auto Note, journal, or continuation helper lines. Auto Note and the source-proven `N` shortcut still determine the typed acknowledgement payload. That surface has no redundant "Classic Textbox" heading or stage-modal minimum size. A negative Classic message uses the same narrative surface without introducing an interaction and remains until the next committed step, matching Castle's no-click path. Textbox history excludes internal event names and sound/picture request diagnostics. The shell may briefly show a native-size app-owned disk or journal glyph at the stage's upper-left only after the host reports the corresponding committed operation.
- A live age-band change uses the inset `Age Update` component, not the Chronicle or Classic textbox. The component renders only typed character/race, resulting band/range, and fifteen-delta payload facts; each current request has one Continue response and independently presents sound 3002.
- Post-battle fumbled-item recovery uses a typed `treasure_distribution` stage component after body count. It displays exact remaining charges and rules-owned recipient availability, then emits assign or leave-behind without mutating inventory directly.
- The same treasure component owns ordinary distribution mode: pending item, pooled denominations, rules-owned recipient availability, Pool/Share, exact Classic Swap increments, stable Detect/Identify controls, and explicit remainder confirmation. Lore caster pickers distinguish authoritative remaining SP from the action cost; a completed lore action stays visibly disabled with its supplied reason while the sibling action remains independently usable if its recomputed caster list permits it. Identified magical items retain both facts in their visible state. Done retains that ordinary component until a committed response either rerenders it or replaces it with the nested completion warning. `LevelUpInteraction` owns result acknowledgement and a full-application-height spell-selection modal using the shared level rail. Both emit typed responses only and remain independently gallery-testable at long-list and inaccessible-action boundaries.
- The Services route owns the ordinary money workspace. Exploration exposes the verified Money bitmap as the ordinary route into Pool/Share/Swap and one contextual location-service command whose title, stable ID, action, and availability come from `GameView`; presentation never infers a shop, temple, or bank from map identity. The workspace renders detached pooled, banked, and personal denominations, character load, Pool/Share, and exact Swap increments; every action uses the core-provided availability and emits one `MONEY_ACTION`. Character selection and Done are presentation-only state and never mutate wealth. The contextual bank uses its own save-owned `BANK` interaction because an active request blocks ordinary intents. No-bank movement departure uses the sibling save-owned `POOLED_WEALTH_DEPARTURE` interaction after its yes/no warning; both render the same detached operations and emit typed responses while the session owns bank import, pool clearing, and exact-once movement resumption.
- The Character route owns a presentation-only Party Order draft behind a compact secondary Reorder control, so formation editing never displaces the ordinary character sheet. Move Up, Move Down, and Cancel never mutate gameplay; Apply emits one complete stable-ID `REORDER_PARTY` permutation. The core owns availability and validation, and a changed campaign or detached member set resets the draft.
- The Allies route is a read-only view of current held-over ally instances. Its menu entry is disabled when the party has none, and list/detail selection remains presentation-only. Bestiary stays unavailable until package content preserves Castle's complete `hd != 0 && !notonmenu` catalog and normalized descriptions; presentation must not replace that contract with discovery state or reachable-monster inference.
- The Character route also owns independent portrait and tactical-icon previews. It sorts each complete detached catalog by that role's source-backed race recommendation, emits one typed stable-ID mutation only on Apply, and makes Discard a presentation-only reset. Active editing never inherits the creator's temporary portrait-to-icon pairing.
- The Journal route keeps player location notes, authored journal entries, and acquired player maps visibly separate. It may edit only the detached current-location note and may browse only the current land/dungeon note stream in source ordinal order. Authored entries render immutable message text in numeric Data SD2 identity order; eligible positive Classic text carries its typed journal choice through acknowledgement without adding another text-well control, while an already-recorded message is read-only. Revert draft is presentation-owned modern wording and emits no intent; it does not claim equivalence to Castle's unresolved dialog exit labels. The acquired-map list preserves unavailable source slots and enables only acquired records; its presenter renders exact PICT assets, signed scrolling text, topology-derived land/dungeon crops, ordered markers, notes, and eligible party marker 138 without mutating simulation. Historical-note topology recentering, darkness display, exact dungeon-map pixels, and styled legacy scrolling text remain explicit gaps.
- The Spells route renders only core-provided field-cast, Make Scroll, and scroll-slot Use actions. It emits the existing typed spell intent with stable character/spell/slot/power identities and never calculates costs, context eligibility, targets, or scroll consumption. Exploration reflects Camp as one persistent bitmap toggle and exposes Rest and Heal only from rules-owned availability. Holding Rest, Heal, or Area Search uses a presentation timer that emits independent typed pulses through footer rerenders; a button release caused only by replacing the footer while the left pointer remains down cannot stop it. The hold stops on physical mouse release, keyboard activation release, focus loss, interaction, or lost availability. Symbol-backed bitmap captions fit within their fixed command cell rather than truncating the command identity. Presentation never advances time, heals, leaves camp, searches, or resumes movement itself. Dungeon instrumentation derives its compact facing label from the detached last-move direction and retains cardinal pointer movement; it never maintains a second facing state.
- A newly mounted route resets its workspace scroll after focus restoration. Route-local rerenders preserve the prior offset after focus restoration, so neither stale workspace state nor focus order can hide the active controls.
- The battle action component renders the session-owned melee/missile mode. It emits the no-cost typed switch response, never offers melee target buttons in missile mode, and labels each rules-owned legal projectile target as Fire. Unsupported or unavailable Fire remains visible with the request's exact reason.
- Active combat keeps its tactical board visible above one full-window-width Classic command deck. A click anywhere outside the active actor's cell is projected through the exact camera transform that rendered the current frame to one of Castle's eight signed directions and submits one adjacent typed move; keyboard/keypad input uses those same directions, and the deck does not duplicate them as permanent buttons. Turn changes restore active-actor focus, and the camera recenters when that actor reaches the visible edge rather than waiting until the actor has left the viewport. Holding Shift reveals core-provided movement costs on adjacent battlefield cells, and opening a spell, item, or target subworkflow suppresses spatial input. Detached combatant facts drive target inspection and source-side Reveal Friends lines; inspection, camera focus, and overlay dismissal remain presentation-owned. Reveal Friends carries a red-hostile/green-friendly/blue-helpless legend, while the separate modern Shift aid carries a gold movement-cost legend; neither is visible by default or styled as the other. The presenter composes battle IDs 1–200 from the detached active-landlook identity and IDs 201–400 from the validated shared PICT 302 atlas, then draws only core-provided actors, targets, and movement availability. It never derives passability, relationship, range, LOS, action cost, or target legality.
- Combat casting follows the Classic staged flow: choose a spell, choose its admitted power, then choose actors or a battlefield center. Actor and repeated-actor targeting happens on request-provided battlefield footprints; spatial spells preview the request's exact Data AD mask under the cursor, but no default or hovered center becomes committed until the player clicks it. Selection order, hover state, cancellation, and preview are presentation-owned, but presentation does not claim legality: confirmation emits the existing typed response and the core validates the selected actor or center once before mutation. Playback uses proven application or scenario-override CIcons for cast/result frames, fixed target-centered numbers, and explicit unavailable diagnostics; it does not name red art as blood or invent an unproven death effect.
- The combat command deck renders the request-ordered current/upcoming initiative sequence with media-catalog combat icons resolved from detached character and monster views, plus core-provided Auto Turn, Delay, Bandage-recipient, and Turn Undead availability and reasons. Its two compact command rows retain fixed slots across actor and availability changes and must fit the default combat region without scrolling; persistent Auto is a separate roster-row toggle carrying only the stable party ID and desired boolean, and its indicator is detached state rather than a presenter-owned preference. The deck may choose a typed Bandage recipient but may not infer bleeding, fresh-turn, priest, undead, allegiance, or once-per-battle eligibility.
- Scenario-picture overlays place a native-scale repeating stone backing under the complete raised bevel. Transparent frame pixels may never expose the map between the surface and bevel.
- Classic opcode 3 carries button labels, not a question prompt. Its yes/no presenter keeps the latest source-authored Classic textbox message visible as context, while an explicit typed request prompt remains authoritative.
- Classic sound playback rotates across four presentation-owned channels. Positive sound requests may overlap; a negative request waits for that channel's completion before the presenter drains later sound events, without introducing a simulation wait.
- Ordinary Swap route entry and exit are presentation-owned lifecycle audio: one deliberate Services-route entry requests button sound 141, stops existing channels before modal sound 3003, and leaving requests sound 141. Same-route rerenders do not replay them, and a Services route opened for a typed Shop, Temple, or Bank interaction is not treated as ordinary Swap. Pool, Share, and transfer sounds remain simulation events.
- Deliberately opening Items or field Spells requests stock workspace sound 20001 or 20002 once after the route changes. Same-route rerenders and automatic workflow routing remain quiet; combat entry and action cues stay in the ordered domain-event stream.
- Starting a physical Rest or Area Search hold requests stock sound 6001 once. Presentation-owned repeat pulses remain quiet until release and a later new hold, matching Castle's sound-before-`StillDown` loop without moving time or search behavior into presentation.
- Cosmetic RNG cannot enter saves, replays, oracle traces, or simulation decisions.

## Work Guidance

- Inventory inspection renders detached Classic record facts and explicit disabled-action reasons. It must not reconstruct bonuses, restrictions, or curse-decoy behavior from package definitions.
- Put tweakable visual values in scene/inspector properties.
- Use MCP to inspect scene trees, properties, errors, runtime state, interactions, and screenshots.

## Verification

- Playable slices follow: open/build scene, inspect editor errors, play scene, run input/test scenario, inspect runtime, capture screenshots, stop scene.
- Runtime MCP tools must never run before `play_scene`.

## Child DOX Index

- `assets/AGENTS.md` owns presentation-owned chrome assets and provenance.
- `controllers/AGENTS.md` owns route-local controller inputs, signals, and mutation boundaries.
- `interaction_components/AGENTS.md` owns typed request-kind control surfaces and exact payload emission.
- `screens/AGENTS.md` owns scene-backed workspace layout, scrolling, and focus containment.

# Presentation asset contract

## Purpose

Own Realmz 2 application chrome assets and their provenance.

## Ownership

- App-owned textures, verified original bitmap controls and mounted/camp map markers, the complete integrated Classic sound and stock music banks, shared item CIcon library, proven built-in combat CIcon families, and bundled fonts used by the Classic-wide shell.
- SpriteCook, donor-commit, Castle resource-fork, Google Fonts, dimension, license, modification, and local hash provenance.

## Local Contracts

- Scenario-owned pictures, icons, portraits, sounds, and map art remain package media. Built-in resource families enter this folder only through an exact-commit catalog with explicit ownership, license, modifications, and byte hashes; scenario packages may override an exact application key.
- The front-door Realmz Rebuilt intro is app-owned project-owner-supplied art, not scenario media. Commit its byte-exact native Ogg Theora/Vorbis stream and record the exact source hash, byte length, dimensions, frame rate, duration, codecs, audio shape, and looping contract in `ui/intro/intro-video.json`. Its app-owned SpriteCook ornament remains separate generated chrome; `ui/spritecook-assets.json` records the style asset, generation job, source hash, transparent-center derivation, dimensions, and production hash.
- Verified base-game UI controls and map markers may enter only through the exact-commit catalog/importer. Preserve each imported source bitmap byte-for-byte. Runtime footer composition may crop or mask the untouched source to isolate its semantic icon while replacing embedded donor captions and hotkeys with live project typography. Record semantic evidence per asset: donor-scene use for controls or pinned Castle resource-fork ownership plus source/control-flow for built-in PICTs and CICNs. A numeric resource ID without its owning fork is insufficient provenance.
- The ordinary map-marker set is exact built-in CICN 175 west, 186 east, and 178 camp. Camp presentation preserves the prior mounted facing for restoration; it never derives or repaints a tent icon.
- Generated structural chrome must contain no text, symbols, scenario content, or executable metadata. App-owned status and command glyphs are separate generated UI categories: each may depict one semantic symbol, contain no embedded words, record its SpriteCook asset/job provenance and exact hashes in `ui/spritecook-assets.json`, and render only at native integer scale. Generate a command glyph only after the stock application library and source control flow prove that no owned icon exists.
- The cataloged spell-target plates remain byte-exact donor evidence. Runtime target badges may key away only their neutral gray plate pixels through `classic_spell_target_text.gdshader`, preserving the original saturated gradient lettering over native Rebuilt inset slate; the source PNGs are never rewritten or presented as application chrome.
- Command bitmap provenance is semantic, not stylistic: current donor controls remain implementation leads unless the catalog proves their Castle resource ownership. App-owned bevel, focus, disabled chrome, and live captions unify footer controls while the compositor samples only the icon portion of untouched donor files. Ordinary Encounter uses exact application PICT 180 as source evidence and masks only the surrounding legacy plate; Heal uses the separately provenance-bound generated glyph because source inspection proves its Castle control has no icon payload. A generated reconstruction cannot be called exact without a supplied reference and explicit provenance.
- Selected SpriteCook chrome records the remote asset ID, generation label, source hash, deterministic derivation, and production hash. Runtime slate uses its deterministic cosine-feathered seamless derivative; frame centers and complete bevel bounds contain that same native-scale tile. The exploration rail is alpha-cropped and reduced to its recorded production dimensions, then centered at no more than 1x over the tiled slate gutter. Opposite tile edges must match exactly, no container may stretch a stone center, and generated frame corners must remain opaque.
- Selected SpriteCook status and command glyphs remain their direct production outputs. The save disk, journal book/quill, and Heal glyph retain their recorded native dimensions and may not be stretched to a shared display size.
- Original controls use nearest-neighbor filtering at exact 1x/2x only. Fonts ship with pinned source, hashes, and licenses and introduce no runtime network dependency. `Theldrow-Classic.fnt` and its atlas are deterministic, metric-preserving conversions of licensed Castle `FONT` 1601; keep that native strike monochrome, nearest-neighbor sampled, and unstretched as reference evidence. `Theldrow-Classic-Vector.ttf` preserves Samuel's scalable CC0 outlines as reference. Runtime Classic text uses deterministic `Theldrow-Rebuilt.ttf`: the approved Pen letter contours, machine-verified production-sheet proportions, sidebearings, and mixed-case optical weight, exact FONT 1601 horizontal advances, zero kerning, and pinned OFL Grenze Gotisch numerals, punctuation, and extended utility glyphs. Numerals keep their Castle advances but are normalized to the declared cap-height figure zone. The reviewed lowercase `h` deliberately overshoots both the cap line and baseline; all other vertical variants follow their declared class zones. Black Chancery, ChicagoFLF, and Castle's Inter Geneva substitute retain their exact pinned bytes. Alegreya remains the readable-mode fallback family.
- The licensed Searching atlas remains byte-exact and records its eight-frame row in the manifest. Exact Torch frame files also remain byte-exact; presentation may key only each asset's documented legacy neutral-gray matte colors while composing them onto Rebuilt chrome.
- Integrated sounds retain exact `snd ` IDs and load from Godot-imported WAV resources. The generated manifest and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` preserve the Castle commit, source fork, copyright, license, and decoding/resampling modification.
- Integrated stock music retains eleven unique Castle modules and loads them from Godot-imported looping Ogg resources. Desert, Swamp, and Snow remain distinct playlist preferences but resolve the Outdoor module; `classic-application-music.json` records exact module commits and hashes, deterministic OpenMPT/FFmpeg conversion settings, output hashes, durations, and the pinned-MADG-to-later-standard-MOD Outdoor replacement. Custom 1–3 are scenario-owned exact resources; never copy them into the application bank.
- Integrated combat CIcons retain exact `cicn` IDs and native dimensions. The selected catalog is limited to source-backed active cues, result effects 159–167, bounded death-effect candidates 2015–2019, and existing spell cast/resolution frames 12000–12127. Standard spells with `lookStart` zero make Castle request the absent 11992–11999 family; presentation reports that exact unavailable identity rather than substituting art. Scenario media overrides the same exact key. Red pixels or numeric adjacency alone do not establish blood, gore, or a semantic identity.
- Integrated item CIcons retain the exact shared Data ID record identity, application-owned stock-supply identities referenced by active-scenario `Data NI`, and Castle's unidentified-range substitutes from `lookupicon`. Core view/request projection selects the player-knowable exact key; Inventory, Equipment, Trade, Shop, and Treasure render that key without exposing its numeric resource ID. Presentation never derives an icon from an item stable ID.
- Keep only selected production assets. Rejected candidates remain external evidence.

## Work Guidance

- Use low-contrast chrome so source art and readable text remain dominant.

## Verification

- Verify each manifest hash, dimension, semantic ID, source commit, rendering rule, and seamless edge pair against the committed file.

## Child DOX Index

- No child AGENTS.md files are currently required.

{

class_name PackageOperationStatus
extends RefCounted

const IDLE: StringName = &"idle"
const RUNNING: StringName = &"running"
const SUCCEEDED: StringName = &"succeeded"
const FAILED: StringName = &"failed"
const CANCELLED: StringName = &"cancelled"

var state: StringName
var phase: StringName
var completed: int
var total: int
var message: String


func _init(operation_state: StringName = IDLE, operation_phase: StringName = &"", completed_units: int = 0, total_units: int = 0, operation_message: String = "") -> void:
	state = operation_state
	phase = operation_phase
	completed = maxi(0, completed_units)
	total = maxi(0, total_units)
	message = operation_message


func is_running() -> bool:
	return state == RUNNING


func progress_ratio() -> float:
	if total <= 0:
		return -1.0
	return clampf(float(completed) / float(total), 0.0, 1.0)

class_name PackageInstallTask
extends RefCounted

const PackageRepositoryScript := preload("res://src/infrastructure/packages/package_repository.gd")
const PackageOperationStatusScript := preload("res://src/infrastructure/packages/package_operation_status.gd")

var _thread := Thread.new()
var _repository: PackageRepository
var _mutex := Mutex.new()
var _state: StringName = PackageOperationStatusScript.IDLE
var _phase: StringName = &""
var _completed: int = 0
var _total: int = 0
var _message: String = ""
var _cancel_requested: bool = false
var _result: PackageInstallResult


func _init(repository: PackageRepository = null) -> void:
	_repository = repository if repository != null else PackageRepositoryScript.new()


func start(source_path: String, install_root: String = "user://packages") -> bool:
	if source_path.is_empty() or snapshot().is_running() or _thread.is_started():
		return false
	_mutex.lock()
	_state = PackageOperationStatusScript.RUNNING
	_phase = &"queued"
	_completed = 0
	_total = 0
	_message = "Preparing campaign…"
	_cancel_requested = false
	_result = null
	_mutex.unlock()
	var error := _thread.start(_run_install.bind(source_path, install_root))
	if error == OK:
		return true
	_mutex.lock()
	_state = PackageOperationStatusScript.FAILED
	_message = "Could not start campaign preparation (error %d)." % error
	_mutex.unlock()
	return false


func cancel() -> void:
	_mutex.lock()
	if _state == PackageOperationStatusScript.RUNNING:
		_cancel_requested = true
		_message = "Cancelling after the current integrity item…"
	_mutex.unlock()


func snapshot() -> RefCounted:
	_mutex.lock()
	var result := PackageOperationStatusScript.new(_state, _phase, _completed, _total, _message)
	_mutex.unlock()
	return result


func take_result() -> PackageInstallResult:
	var current := snapshot()
	if current.is_running() or current.state == PackageOperationStatusScript.IDLE:
		return null
	_join_thread()
	_mutex.lock()
	var result := _result
	_result = null
	_state = PackageOperationStatusScript.IDLE
	_phase = &""
	_completed = 0
	_total = 0
	_message = ""
	_mutex.unlock()
	return result


func shutdown() -> void:
	cancel()
	_join_thread()


func _run_install(source_path: String, install_root: String) -> void:
	var result := _repository.install_package(source_path, install_root, _on_progress, _is_cancel_requested)
	_mutex.lock()
	_result = result
	if result != null and result.is_ok():
		_state = PackageOperationStatusScript.SUCCEEDED
		_phase = &"complete"
		_completed = 1
		_total = 1
		_message = "Campaign ready."
	elif result != null and result.error_code == &"package_cancelled":
		_state = PackageOperationStatusScript.CANCELLED
		_message = "Campaign preparation cancelled."
	else:
		_state = PackageOperationStatusScript.FAILED
		_message = result.error_message if result != null else "Campaign preparation failed."
	_mutex.unlock()


func _on_progress(operation_phase: StringName, completed_units: int, total_units: int) -> void:
	_mutex.lock()
	_phase = operation_phase
	_completed = completed_units
	_total = total_units
	if not _cancel_requested:
		_message = _message_for(operation_phase, completed_units, total_units)
	_mutex.unlock()


func _is_cancel_requested() -> bool:
	_mutex.lock()
	var requested := _cancel_requested
	_mutex.unlock()
	return requested


func _join_thread() -> void:
	if _thread.is_started():
		_thread.wait_to_finish()


static func _message_for(operation_phase: StringName, completed_units: int, total_units: int) -> String:
	match operation_phase:
		&"opening": return "Opening campaign package…"
		&"checking-install": return "Opening installed campaign…"
		&"validating-source": return "Checking external package before installation…"
		&"validating-integrity": return "Checking external package files %d of %d…" % [completed_units, total_units]
		&"constructing-content": return "Loading compiled Realmz content…"
		&"copying-package": return "Installing immutable package…"
		&"validating-install": return "Checking installed copy…"
		&"complete": return "Campaign ready."
	return "Preparing campaign…"

class_name FastSpellDock
extends PanelContainer

signal slot_activated(slot_index: int)

const FRAME_DURATION_SECONDS := 0.12
const DOCK_HEIGHT := 76.0
const MIN_SLOT_WIDTH := 44.0
const MAX_SLOT_WIDTH := 68.0
const SLOT_SEPARATION := 4.0

var _stage_rect := Rect2()
var _row: HBoxContainer
var _buttons: Array[Button] = []
var _previews: Array[TextureRect] = []
var _frames_by_entry: Array = []
var _frame_index := 0
var _frame_elapsed := 0.0
var _has_assigned_binding := false


func _init() -> void:
	name = "FastSpellDock"
	theme_type_variation = &"ClassicInset"
	mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
	z_index = 90
	visible = false
	set_process(false)
	_row = HBoxContainer.new()
	_row.name = "FastSpellDockSlots"
	_row.add_theme_constant_override("separation", int(SLOT_SEPARATION))
	add_child(_row)


func configure(bindings: Array[InteractionRequestValue.FastSpell], animation_frames: Dictionary) -> void:
	_clear_entries()
	_has_assigned_binding = false
	for slot_index: int in mini(10, bindings.size()):
		var binding := bindings[slot_index]
		if binding.spell_id.is_empty():
			continue
		_has_assigned_binding = true
		_add_binding(slot_index, binding, animation_frames.get(binding.spell_id, []) as Array)
	_apply_layout()


func set_stage_rect(stage_rect: Rect2) -> void:
	_stage_rect = stage_rect
	_apply_layout()


func set_held(held: bool) -> bool:
	visible = held and _has_assigned_binding and not _buttons.is_empty()
	set_process(visible)
	if visible:
		_frame_elapsed = 0.0
	return _has_assigned_binding


func has_assigned_binding() -> bool:
	return _has_assigned_binding


func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	_frame_elapsed += delta
	if _frame_elapsed < FRAME_DURATION_SECONDS:
		return
	_frame_elapsed = fmod(_frame_elapsed, FRAME_DURATION_SECONDS)
	_frame_index += 1
	for index: int in _previews.size():
		var frames: Array = _frames_by_entry[index]
		if not frames.is_empty():
			_previews[index].texture = frames[_frame_index % frames.size()] as Texture2D


func _add_binding(slot_index: int, binding: InteractionRequestValue.FastSpell, frames: Array) -> void:
	var button := Button.new()
	button.name = "FastSpellDockSlot%d" % slot_index
	button.theme_type_variation = &"ClassicTheldrowButton"
	button.disabled = not binding.enabled
	button.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_ALL
	button.tooltip_text = "%s • Power %d%s" % [binding.spell_name, binding.power, "" if binding.enabled else " • %s" % binding.reason]
	button.pressed.connect(func() -> void: slot_activated.emit(slot_index))
	_row.add_child(button)
	_buttons.append(button)

	var content := VBoxContainer.new()
	content.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	content.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT, Control.PRESET_MODE_MINSIZE, 4)
	content.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 0)
	button.add_child(content)

	var preview := TextureRect.new()
	preview.name = "FastSpellDockPreview%d" % slot_index
	preview.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0.0, 42.0)
	preview.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	preview.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	preview.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
	preview.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
	preview.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
	preview.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	if not frames.is_empty():
		preview.texture = frames[0] as Texture2D
	content.add_child(preview)
	_previews.append(preview)
	_frames_by_entry.append(frames)

	var key_label := Label.new()
	key_label.name = "FastSpellDockKey%d" % slot_index
	key_label.text = "%s · P%d" % ["0" if slot_index == 9 else str(slot_index + 1), binding.power]
	key_label.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	key_label.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	key_label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 13)
	key_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color("f0ce59") if binding.enabled else Color("8c8170"))
	content.add_child(key_label)


func _apply_layout() -> void:
	if _stage_rect.size.x <= 0.0 or _buttons.is_empty():
		return
	var count := _buttons.size()
	var available_width := maxf(1.0, _stage_rect.size.x - 24.0 - SLOT_SEPARATION * float(count - 1))
	var slot_width := clampf(floorf(available_width / float(count)), MIN_SLOT_WIDTH, MAX_SLOT_WIDTH)
	for button: Button in _buttons:
		button.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(slot_width, DOCK_HEIGHT - 10.0)
	var dock_width := slot_width * float(count) + SLOT_SEPARATION * float(count - 1) + 12.0
	size = Vector2(dock_width, DOCK_HEIGHT)
	position = Vector2(_stage_rect.position.x + (_stage_rect.size.x - dock_width) * 0.5, _stage_rect.end.y - DOCK_HEIGHT - 8.0)


func _clear_entries() -> void:
	_buttons.clear()
	_previews.clear()
	_frames_by_entry.clear()
	_frame_index = 0
	_frame_elapsed = 0.0
	for child: Node in _row.get_children():
		_row.remove_child(child)
		child.queue_free()

const SpellSelectionChrome := preload("res://src/presentation/controllers/classic_spell_selection_chrome.gd")

const GOLD := Color("e5c45c")
const CYAN := Color("8fcfd1")
const MUTED := Color("aeb6ba")

var _game_view: GameView
var _media: ClassicMediaCatalog
var _spell_buttons: Dictionary = {}
var _selected_spell_ids: Array[String] = []

func configure(game_view: GameView, media: ClassicMediaCatalog) -> void:
	_game_view = game_view
	_media = media


func build(request: InteractionRequest) -> void:
	var body := request.body as InteractionRequest.LevelUpRequestBody
	if body == null:
		add_hint("The level-up request is malformed.")
		return
	size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0.0, 320.0)
	add_theme_constant_override("separation", 6)
	if body.mode == &"result":
		_build_result(body)
	elif body.mode == &"spell-selection":
		_build_spell_selection(body)
	else:
		add_hint("The level-up request is malformed.")


func _build_result(body: InteractionRequest.LevelUpRequestBody) -> void:
	if body.character_id.is_empty() or body.gains == null:
		add_hint("The level result is unavailable.")
		return
	_build_header("Level Gained", "%s reached level %d" % [body.character_name, body.level])
	var columns := HBoxContainer.new()

	columns.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	columns.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
	add_child(columns)
	_build_level_identity(columns, body)
	_build_gain_record(columns, body)
	_build_result_action(columns, body)


func _build_level_identity(parent: HBoxContainer, body: InteractionRequest.LevelUpRequestBody) -> void:
	var content := _pane(parent, "LevelIdentity", "Adventurer", 0.8)
	var portrait := TextureRect.new()
	portrait.name = "LevelPortrait"
	portrait.texture = _portrait(body.character_id)
	portrait.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
	portrait.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
	portrait.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
	portrait.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(160.0, 220.0)
	portrait.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	content.add_child(portrait)
	content.add_child(_label(body.character_name, GOLD, 18))
	content.add_child(_label("Level %d" % body.level, CYAN, 16))
	if portrait.texture == null:
		portrait.custom_minimum_size.y = 80.0
		content.add_child(_label("No exact portrait is available.", MUTED, 13))


func _build_gain_record(parent: HBoxContainer, body: InteractionRequest.LevelUpRequestBody) -> void:
	var content := _pane(parent, "LevelGains", "Committed Gains", 1.25)
	var grid := GridContainer.new()
	grid.name = "LevelGainGrid"
	grid.columns = 2
	grid.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	grid.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	grid.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 6)
	grid.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 6)
	content.add_child(grid)
	for record: Dictionary in [
		{"label": "Stamina", "value": body.gains.stamina},
		{"label": "Spell Points", "value": body.gains.spell_points},
		{"label": "To Hit", "value": body.gains.to_hit},
		{"label": "Magic Resistance", "value": body.gains.magic_resistance},
	]:
		var card := PanelContainer.new()
		card.theme_type_variation = &"ClassicInset"
		card.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
		card.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
		grid.add_child(card)
		var facts := VBoxContainer.new()
		facts.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
		facts.add_child(_label(String(record.label), MUTED, 14))
		facts.add_child(_label("%+d" % int(record.value), GOLD, 24))
		card.add_child(facts)


func _build_result_action(parent: HBoxContainer, body: InteractionRequest.LevelUpRequestBody) -> void:
	var content := _pane(parent, "LevelContinuation", "Adventure", 0.85)
	content.add_child(_label("These gains are already committed to the adventure.", MUTED, 14))
	var spacer := Control.new()
	spacer.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	content.add_child(spacer)
	var button := add_response_to(content, "Continue", InteractionResponse.LevelUpBody.new(&"continue", body.character_id))
	button.name = "LevelContinue"
	button.custom_minimum_size.y = 44.0


func _build_spell_selection(body: InteractionRequest.LevelUpRequestBody) -> void:
	if body.character_id.is_empty():
		add_hint("The spell-selection request is unavailable.")
		return
	_build_header("Learn Spells", body.character_name)
	_selected_spell_ids.clear()
	for spell: InteractionRequestValue.SpellChoice in body.spells:
		if spell.selected:
			_selected_spell_ids.append(spell.id)
	var available_levels := _available_spell_levels(body)
	_selected_level = available_levels[0] if not available_levels.is_empty() else 1
	var columns := HBoxContainer.new()
	columns.name = "LevelSpellColumns"
	columns.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	columns.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	columns.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
	add_child(columns)
	_build_spell_level_rail(columns, body, available_levels)
	var list_content := _pane(columns, "LevelSpellCandidates", "", 1.45)
	_spell_list_heading = _label("", GOLD, 17)
	_spell_list_heading.theme_type_variation = &"ClassicHeading"
	list_content.add_child(_spell_list_heading)
	var scroll := ScrollContainer.new()
	scroll.name = "LevelSpellScroll"
	scroll.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	scroll.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	list_content.add_child(scroll)
	_spell_list = VBoxContainer.new()
	_spell_list.name = "LevelSpellList"
	_spell_list.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	_spell_list.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 3)
	scroll.add_child(_spell_list)
	_rebuild_spell_list(body)
	var action_content := _pane(columns, "LevelSpellAllowance", "Spell Record", 0.9)
	_selection_summary = _label("", CYAN, 16)
	action_content.add_child(_selection_summary)
	var record := PanelContainer.new()
	record.name = "LevelSelectedSpellRecord"
	record.theme_type_variation = &"ClassicInset"
	record.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	action_content.add_child(record)
	var record_content := VBoxContainer.new()
	record_content.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
	record.add_child(record_content)

class_name EncounterInteraction
extends InteractionComponent

const ClassicSpellLevelScript := preload("res://src/presentation/classic_spell_level.gd")
const SpellSelectionChrome := preload("res://src/presentation/controllers/classic_spell_selection_chrome.gd")

var _body: InteractionRequest.ComplexEncounterRequestBody
var _context: VBoxContainer
var _choice_actions: Array[InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction] = []
var _word_action: InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction
var _item_action: InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction
var _spell_action: InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction
var _thief_action: InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction
var _back_action: InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction
var _catalog_kind: StringName = &""
var _catalog_entries: Array[InteractionRequestValue.EncounterCatalogEntry] = []
var _catalog_selection: int = 0
var _catalog_record: VBoxContainer
var _catalog_list: VBoxContainer
var _catalog_buttons: Array[Button] = []
var _catalog_level: int = 1
var _catalog_level_buttons: Array[Button] = []


func build(request: InteractionRequest) -> void:
	_body = request.body as InteractionRequest.ComplexEncounterRequestBody
	if _body == null:
		return
	_classify_actions()
	var command_deck := PanelContainer.new()
	command_deck.name = "EncounterCommandDeck"
	command_deck.theme_type_variation = &"ClassicInset"
	command_deck.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	add_child(command_deck)
	var strip := GridContainer.new()
	strip.name = "EncounterCommandStrip"
	strip.columns = 6
	strip.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	strip.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 6)
	command_deck.add_child(strip)
	_add_command(strip, &"action", &"encounter.action", "Action", not _choice_actions.is_empty(), "No authored actions are available.")
	_add_command(strip, &"item", &"encounter.items", "Items", _item_action != null and not _body.items.is_empty(), "No eligible item is available.")
	_add_command(strip, &"thief", &"encounter.skills", "Skills", _thief_action != null, "No thief action is available.")
	_add_command(strip, &"word", &"encounter.speak", "Speak", _word_action != null, "This encounter accepts no spoken response.")
	_add_command(strip, &"spell", &"command.spells", "Spells", _spell_action != null and not _body.spells.is_empty(), "No eligible spell is available.")
	_add_command(strip, &"back", &"encounter.stop", "Stop", _back_action != null, "This encounter cannot be left yet.")
	var context_deck := PanelContainer.new()
	context_deck.name = "EncounterContextDeck"
	context_deck.theme_type_variation = &"ClassicInset"
	context_deck.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	context_deck.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	add_child(context_deck)
	_context = VBoxContainer.new()
	_context.name = "EncounterContextPane"
	_context.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	_context.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	_context.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 5)
	context_deck.add_child(_context)
	_show_first_available()


func handle_back() -> bool:
	if not _catalog_kind.is_empty():
		_cancel_catalog()
		return true
	if _back_action != null:
		response_body_submitted.emit(InteractionResponse.ComplexEncounterBody.new(&"back"))
		return true
	return false


func _classify_actions() -> void:
	for entry: InteractionRequestValue.EncounterAction in _body.actions:
		match entry.kind:
			&"choice": _choice_actions.append(entry)
			&"word": _word_action = entry
			&"item": _item_action = entry
			&"spell": _spell_action = entry
			&"thief": _thief_action = entry
			&"back": _back_action = entry


func _add_command(parent: GridContainer, mode: StringName, asset_id: StringName, label: String, enabled: bool, reason: String) -> void:
	var button := ClassicBitmapButton.new()
	button.name = "EncounterCommand%s" % String(mode).capitalize()
	button.configure({"id": mode, "asset_id": asset_id, "tooltip": label, "accelerator": ""}, 1)
	button.disabled = not enabled
	if not enabled:
		button.tooltip_text = reason
	button.command_requested.connect(_on_command_requested)
	parent.add_child(button)


func _on_command_requested(mode: StringName) -> void:
	match mode:
		&"action", &"item", &"word", &"spell": _show_mode(mode)
		&"thief": response_body_submitted.emit(InteractionResponse.ComplexEncounterBody.new(&"thief"))
		&"back": response_body_submitted.emit(InteractionResponse.ComplexEncounterBody.new(&"back"))


func _show_first_available() -> void:
	for mode: StringName in [&"action", &"item", &"word", &"spell"]:
		if _mode_available(mode):
			_show_mode(mode)
			return
	var label := Label.new()
	label.text = "Choose an available encounter command."
	label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color("d5b45d"))
	_context.add_child(label)


func _mode_available(mode: StringName) -> bool:
	match mode:
		&"action": return not _choice_actions.is_empty()
		&"item": return _item_action != null and not _body.items.is_empty()
		&"word": return _word_action != null
		&"spell": return _spell_action != null and not _body.spells.is_empty()
	return false


func _show_mode(mode: StringName) -> void:
	_clear_context()
	match mode:
		&"action": _show_choices()
		&"item": _show_catalog(&"item", _body.items)
		&"word": _show_word()
		&"spell": _show_catalog(&"spell", _body.spells)


func _show_choices() -> void:
	var grid := GridContainer.new()
	grid.name = "EncounterChoiceGrid"
	grid.columns = 2 if _choice_actions.size() > 1 else 1
	grid.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	grid.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 6)
	grid.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 5)
	_context.add_child(grid)
	for index: int in _choice_actions.size():
		var entry := _choice_actions[index]
		var response := InteractionResponse.ComplexEncounterBody.new(&"choice", entry.slot)
		add_response_to(grid, "%d · %s" % [index + 1, entry.label], response)


func _show_word() -> void:
	var workspace := VBoxContainer.new()
	workspace.name = "EncounterWordWorkspace"
	workspace.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	workspace.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 3)
	_context.add_child(workspace)
	var entry_row := HBoxContainer.new()
	entry_row.name = "EncounterWordActions"
	entry_row.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 6)
	workspace.add_child(entry_row)
	var label := Label.new()
	label.text = "Response"
	label.custom_minimum_size.x = 72.0
	entry_row.add_child(label)
	var word := LineEdit.new()
	word.name = "EncounterWord"
	word.placeholder_text = "Word or phrase"
